title.zh: 卷三百十八 列傳第七十七 張方平 王拱辰 張昪 趙槩 胡宿
title.en: Volume 318 Biographies 77: Zhang Fangping, Wang Gongchen, Zhang Bian, Zhao Gai, Hu Su
title.raw: 卷三百十八 列傳第七十七 張方平 王拱辰 張昪 趙槩 胡宿 Volume 318 Biographies 77: Zhang Fangping, Wang Gongchen, Zhang Bian, Zhao Gai, Hu Su

sentences.zh: 張方平

translations.literal: Zhang Fangping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fangping

sentences.zh: 張方平，字安道，南京人。

translations.literal: Zhang Fangping, courtesy name Andao, was a native of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fangping, styled Andao, was from Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 少穎悟絕倫，家貧無書，從人假三史，旬日即歸之，曰：「吾已得其詳矣。」

translations.literal: In youth he was exceptionally intelligent beyond compare; his family was poor and had no books. He borrowed the Three Histories from someone, and within ten days returned them, saying: "I have already mastered their details."
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was brilliantly gifted beyond his peers. His family was poor and owned no books, so he borrowed the Three Histories from someone; within ten days he returned them, saying, "I have already taken in all their particulars."

sentences.zh: 凡書皆一閱不再讀，宋綬、蔡齊以為天下奇才。

translations.literal: With every book he read it once and never read it again. Song Shou and Cai Qi regarded him as a rare genius under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He never needed to read any book more than once. Song Shou and Cai Qi considered him a wonder of the age.

sentences.zh: 舉茂材異等，為校書郎、知崐山縣。

translations.literal: He was recommended as extraordinary talent of outstanding grade and appointed Proofreader and magistrate of Kunshan County.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as extraordinary talent of the highest grade, he was made Proofreader and magistrate of Kunshan County.

sentences.zh: 又中賢良方正，選遷著作佐郎、通判睦州。

translations.literal: He also passed the evaluation for worthy and upright men and was selected and promoted to Assistant Compiler and deputy prefect of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also passed the worthy-and-upright examination and was promoted to Assistant Compiler and vice-prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 趙元昊且叛，為嫚書來，規得譴絕以激使其眾。

translations.literal: Zhao Yuanhao was about to rebel and sent an insulting letter, planning to obtain dismissal and severance of relations so as to incite his followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yuanhao was on the verge of rebellion, he sent an insulting letter, scheming to draw down imperial reproach and a break in relations so as to stir up his people.

sentences.zh: 方平請：「順適其意，使未有以發，得歲月之頃，以其間選將厲士，堅城除器，為不可勝以待之。

translations.literal: Fangping petitioned: "Accommodate his intent so that he has no occasion to act, gaining the span of months and years; in the interval select generals and train troops, strengthen fortifications and ready weapons, and make ourselves invincible in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping petitioned: "Humor his intent so that he has no pretext to act, and buy the span of months and years. In that interval select generals, harden the troops, strengthen the walls, and ready the weapons, until we are invincible and waiting for him.

sentences.zh: 雖終於必叛，而兵出無名，吏士不直其上，難以決勝。

translations.literal: Even if he ultimately must rebel, if our troops take the field without a righteous cause and officers and soldiers do not find their superiors just, it will be hard to achieve victory.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he must rebel in the end, if our army marches without a righteous cause and officers and men do not find their superiors upright, it will be hard to win a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 小國用兵三年，而不見勝負，不折則破；

translations.literal: When a small state wages war for three years without seeing victory or defeat, if it is not broken it will be shattered;
translations.idiomatic: When a small state wages war for three years without a clear outcome, if it is not worn down it will be shattered;

sentences.zh: 我以全制其後，必勝之道也。」

translations.literal: we may use our wholeness to control what follows—that is the sure path to victory."
translations.idiomatic: we may then use our intact strength to control what follows—that is the sure path to victory."

sentences.zh: 時天下全盛，皆謂其論出姑息，決計用兵。

translations.literal: At the time the empire was in full prosperity, and all regarded his argument as born of excessive indulgence; the decision was made to use force.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the empire was at its height, and all called his argument mere indulgence; the court resolved on war.

sentences.zh: 方平上《平戎十策》，以為：「入寇當自延、渭，巢穴之守必虛。

translations.literal: Fangping submitted the "Ten Stratagems for Pacifying the Barbarians," holding that: "If they invade it will be from Yan and Wei, and the defense of their nest must surely be weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping submitted the Ten Stratagems for Pacifying the Barbarians, arguing: "If they raid, they will come from Yan and Wei, and the defense of their stronghold must be left thin.

sentences.zh: 宜屯兵河東，卷甲而趨之，所謂攻其所必救，形格勢禁之道也。」

translations.literal: We should station troops in Hedong and march swiftly thither—what is called striking where they must rescue, the way of checking form and restraining momentum."
translations.idiomatic: We should mass troops in Hedong and march swiftly thither—what is called striking where they must rescue, the method of checking their form and restraining their momentum."

sentences.zh: 宰相呂夷簡善其策而不果行。

translations.literal: The chief councilor Lü Yijian approved his plan but it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Lü Yijian approved his plan, but it was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 當召試館職，仁宗曰：「是非兩策制科者乎？

translations.literal: When he was to be summoned for examination for an academy post, Renzong said: "Is this not the man of the two-policy policy examination?
translations.idiomatic: When he was to be summoned for examination for an academy post, Renzong said, "Is this not the man who passed the two-policy policy examination?

sentences.zh: 何試也？」

translations.literal: Why test him?"
translations.idiomatic: Why test him?"

sentences.zh: 命直集賢院，俄知諫院。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve directly in the Academy of Worthies, and soon made director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve directly in the Academy of Worthies, and soon made director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇邊，方平首乞合樞密之職於中書，以通謀議。

translations.literal: When the Xia raided the frontier, Fangping was the first to request merging the duties of the Military Affairs Commission with the Secretariat so that deliberation might be unified.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia raided the frontier, Fangping was the first to ask that the duties of the Military Affairs Commission be merged with the Secretariat so that planning might flow through a single channel.

sentences.zh: 帝然之，遂以宰相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: The emperor approved, and consequently the chief councilor also held the post of commissioner of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and thereafter the chief councilor also served as commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時調諸道弓手，刺其壯者為宣毅、保捷，方平連疏爭之，弗聽。

translations.literal: At the time bowmen were levied from all circuits, and the able-bodied were selected for the Xuan Yi and Bao Jie units. Fangping submitted repeated memorials objecting, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bowmen were levied from every circuit, and the able-bodied were picked for the Xuan Yi and Bao Jie corps. Fangping submitted repeated memorials in protest, but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 既而兩軍驕甚，合二十餘萬，皆市人不可用，如方平言。

translations.literal: Before long the two armies grew extremely arrogant; together they numbered more than two hundred thousand, all townsmen unusable for combat, just as Fangping had said.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the two corps grew insufferably arrogant; together they numbered more than two hundred thousand men, all townsmen unfit for war, just as Fangping had warned.

sentences.zh: 夏竦節制陝西並護諸將，四路以稟覆失事機，且詔使出師，逗遛不行。

translations.literal: Xia Song directed Shaanxi and supervised all generals; the four circuits lost their timing through reporting and awaiting reply, and moreover envoys ordered to take the field dallied and would not march.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song directed Shaanxi and oversaw all the generals. The four circuits lost their timing through reporting up and waiting for reply, and even envoys ordered to take the field dallied and would not march.

sentences.zh: 及豐州陷，劉平等覆師，主帥皆坐譴，竦獨不預，方平劾罷之，而請四路帥臣，各自任戰守。

translations.literal: When Feng Prefecture fell and Liu Ping and others lost their army, the commanders were all punished; Xia alone was not implicated. Fangping impeached him and had him removed, and requested that the commanders of the four circuits each bear responsibility for fighting and defense on their own.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Prefecture fell and Liu Ping and others were destroyed, the commanders were all punished; Xia alone was not implicated. Fangping impeached him and had him removed, and asked that the commanders of the four circuits each bear full responsibility for fighting and defense on their own.

sentences.zh: 西師久未解，元昊亦困弊，方平言：「陛下猶天地父母也，豈與犬豕豺狼較乎？

translations.literal: The western campaign was long unsettled and Yuanhao was also worn down. Fangping said: "Your Majesty is still Heaven and Earth, father and mother—how can you contend with dogs, pigs, and wolves?
translations.idiomatic: The western campaign dragged on without resolution, and Yuanhao too was exhausted. Fangping said, "Your Majesty is still Heaven and Earth, father and mother—how can you measure yourself against dogs, pigs, and wolves?

sentences.zh: 願因郊赦，引咎示信，開其自新之路。」

translations.literal: I hope that on the occasion of the suburban amnesty you may acknowledge fault and show good faith, opening a path for them to renew themselves."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that on the occasion of the suburban amnesty you acknowledge fault and show good faith, opening a path for them to renew themselves."

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「是吾心也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said gladly: "That is my own heart."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said gladly, "That is my own heart."

sentences.zh: 是歲，改慶曆赦書，敕邊吏通其善意，元昊竟降。

translations.literal: That year the Qingli amnesty edict was revised, border officials were ordered to convey this goodwill, and Yuanhao eventually submitted.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Qingli amnesty edict was revised, border officials were ordered to convey this goodwill, and Yuanhao eventually submitted.

sentences.zh: 既以修起居注使契丹。

translations.literal: Subsequently, as compiler of the Daily Records, he was sent as envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent as envoy to the Khitan in his capacity as compiler of the Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 契丹主顧左右曰：「有臣如此，佳哉！」

translations.literal: The Khitan sovereign turned to those about him and said: "To have a minister such as this—how excellent!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sovereign turned to those beside him and said, "To have a minister such as this—how excellent!"

sentences.zh: 騎而擊毬於前，酌玉卮飲之，且贈以所乘馬。

translations.literal: He rode forth and played cuju before him, poured wine from a jade goblet for him to drink, and moreover gave him the horse he himself rode.
translations.idiomatic: He rode out and played cuju before him, poured wine from a jade goblet for him to drink, and gave him the horse on which he himself had ridden.

sentences.zh: 還，知制誥，權知開封府。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Drafting Edict-er and acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Drafting Edict-er and acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 府事叢集，前尹率書板識之，方平獨默記決遣，無少差忘。

translations.literal: The prefectural business was piled together; previous prefects generally noted matters on boards, but Fangping alone memorized cases and decided them, without the least error or lapse.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural business piled up in heaps; previous prefects usually wrote matters on boards, but Fangping alone committed them to memory and decided them, without the least slip or lapse.

sentences.zh: 進翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 元昊既臣，而與契丹有隙，來請絕其使，議者不可。

translations.literal: Once Yuanhao had submitted but had a rift with the Khitan and came to request cutting off their envoys, discussants said this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuanhao had submitted but had fallen out with the Khitan, he asked that their envoys be cut off; those who debated the matter said this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 方平曰：「得新附之小羌，失久和之強敵，非計也。

translations.literal: Fangping said: "To gain a newly submitted petty Qiang while losing a long-peaceful powerful foe is no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping said, "To gain a newly submitted petty Qiang while losing a long-peaceful powerful foe is no plan at all.

sentences.zh: 宜賜元昊詔，使之審處，但嫌隙朝除，則封冊暮下。

translations.literal: We should bestow an edict upon Yuanhao ordering him to weigh the matter carefully: only let enmity be removed by morning and investiture will issue by evening.
translations.idiomatic: We should send Yuanhao an edict ordering him to weigh the matter carefully: let the rift be removed by morning, and investiture will issue by evening.

sentences.zh: 如此，於西、北為兩得矣。」

translations.literal: In this way we may gain on both west and north."
translations.idiomatic: In this way we may gain on both the western and northern fronts.

sentences.zh: 時韙其謀。

translations.literal: At the time his plan was approved.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 拜御史中丞，改三司使。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor-in-chief and transferred to commissioner of the Three Fiscal Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed censor-in-chief and transferred to commissioner of the Three Fiscal Commissions.

sentences.zh: 初，王拱辰議榷河北鹽，方平見曰：「河北再榷鹽，何也？」

translations.literal: Initially Wang Gongchen proposed state monopoly of salt in Hebei. Fangping had audience and said: "To monopolize salt in Hebei again—why?"
translations.idiomatic: At first Wang Gongchen proposed a state salt monopoly in Hebei. Fangping had audience and said, "To monopolize salt in Hebei again—why?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「始立法耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is only to establish the law."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "It is only to establish the law."

sentences.zh: 方平曰：「昔周世宗以鹽課均之稅中，今兩稅鹽錢是也。

translations.literal: Fangping said: "Formerly Emperor Shizong of Zhou folded salt levies into the tax assessment; today's salt money in the two taxes is that very thing.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping said, "Formerly Emperor Shizong of Zhou folded salt levies into the tax assessment; the salt money in today's two taxes is exactly that.

sentences.zh: 豈非再榷乎？」

translations.literal: Is this not a second monopoly?"
translations.idiomatic: Is this not a second monopoly?"

sentences.zh: 帝驚悟，方平請直降手詔罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor started in astonishment and understood; Fangping requested that the emperor personally issue a handwritten edict to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started in astonishment and understood; Fangping asked that the emperor personally issue a handwritten edict to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 河朔父老迎拜於澶州，為佛老會七日，以報上恩，事具《食貨志》。

translations.literal: The elders of Heshuo came to bow in welcome at Dazhou, held Buddhist and Daoist assemblies for seven days to repay imperial grace—the full account is in the Monographs on Food and Goods.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of Heshuo came to bow in welcome at Dazhou and held Buddhist and Daoist assemblies for seven days to repay imperial grace; the full account is in the Monographs on Food and Goods.

sentences.zh: 加端明殿學士、判太常寺。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title academician of the Duanming Hall and concurrently directed the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title of academician of the Duanming Hall and concurrently directed the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 禁中衛卒夜變，帝旦語二府，獎張貴妃扈蹕功。

translations.literal: Palace guards mutinied at night; at dawn the emperor told the two councils and praised Noble Consort Zhang's merit in escorting him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards mutinied at night; at dawn the emperor told the two councils and praised Noble Consort Zhang for escorting him in the disturbance.

sentences.zh: 夏竦即倡言：「當求所以尊異之禮。」

translations.literal: Xia Song immediately advocated: "We should seek rites by which to honor and distinguish her."
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song immediately advocated, "We should seek rites by which to honor and distinguish her."

sentences.zh: 方平聞之，謂陳執中曰：「漢馮婕妤身當猛獸，不聞有所尊異；

translations.literal: Hearing this, Fangping said to Chen Zhizhong: "In Han, Consort Feng Jieyu shielded the emperor from a wild beast, yet one never hears of special honors for it;
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Fangping said to Chen Zhizhong, "In Han, Consort Feng Jieyu shielded the emperor from a wild beast, yet one never hears of special honors for it;

sentences.zh: 且皇后在而尊貴妃，古無是事。

translations.literal: moreover, with the empress present to exalt a noble consort—there is no such thing in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: moreover, with the empress still present to exalt a noble consort—there is no such thing in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 果行之，天下之責，將萃於公矣。」

translations.literal: If you truly carry this out, the blame of all under Heaven will gather upon you."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly carry this out, the blame of all under Heaven will gather upon you.

sentences.zh: 執中瞿然而罷。

translations.literal: Chen Zhizhong started back and dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhizhong started back and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝以豐財省費訪群臣，方平既條對，又獨上數千言，大略以為：「祥符以來，務為姑息，漸失祖宗之舊。

translations.literal: When the emperor sought the ministers' counsel on enriching the treasury and saving expense, Fangping both replied item by item and separately submitted several thousand characters, in outline holding that: "Since the Xiangfu era there has been a pursuit of indulgent ease, gradually losing the institutions of the founding ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sought the ministers' counsel on enriching the treasury and saving expense, Fangping both replied item by item and separately submitted several thousand characters, arguing in outline that since the Xiangfu era the court had pursued indulgent ease and had gradually lost the institutions of the founding ancestors.

sentences.zh: 取士、任子、磨勘、遷補之法壞，命將養兵，皆非舊律。

translations.literal: The methods of recruiting scholars, appointing sons by privilege, merit review, and advancement are ruined; appointing generals and training troops—none follow the old rules.
translations.idiomatic: The methods of recruiting scholars, appointing sons by privilege, merit review, and advancement have broken down; appointing generals and training troops no longer follow the old rules.

sentences.zh: 國用既窘，則政出多門；

translations.literal: When state revenue is already straitened, policy issues from many gates;
translations.idiomatic: When state revenue is already straitened, policy issues from many gates;

sentences.zh: 大商豪民乘隙射利，而茶鹽香礬之法亂。

translations.literal: great merchants and powerful families seize gaps to seek profit, and the laws on tea, salt, incense, and alum are in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: great merchants and powerful families seize every opening for profit, and the laws on tea, salt, incense, and alum fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 此治忽盛衰之本，不可以不急。」

translations.literal: These are the roots of governance's rise and fall, flourishing and decline, and cannot be treated as unurgent."
translations.idiomatic: These are the roots of whether governance flourishes or fails, and they cannot be treated as anything but urgent.

sentences.zh: 帝覽對甚悅，且大用，會判官楊儀得罪，坐與交，出知滁州。

translations.literal: The emperor read the reply with great pleasure and was about to employ him greatly, but the judge Yang Yi offended the court; because of association with him Fangping was sent out as prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the reply with great pleasure and was about to employ him greatly, but the judge Yang Yi offended the court; because Fangping associated with him, he was sent out as prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，知江寧府，入判流內銓。

translations.literal: Before long he was prefect of Jiangning and entered to direct the Inner Flow Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was prefect of Jiangning, then entered court to direct the Inner Flow Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 以侍講學士知滑州，徙益州。

translations.literal: As lecturer-in-waiting academician he was made prefect of Huazhou, then transferred to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: As lecturer-in-waiting academician he was made prefect of Huazhou, then transferred to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 未至，或扇言儂智高在南詔，將入寇，攝守亟調兵築城，日夜不得息，民大驚擾。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, some spread word that Nong Zhigao in Nanzhao was about to invade; the acting prefect hastily levied troops and built walls, allowing no rest day or night, and the people were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, some spread word that Nong Zhigao in Nanzhao was about to invade; the acting prefect hastily levied troops and built walls, allowing no rest day or night, and the people were thrown into great alarm.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，發陝西步騎兵仗，絡繹往戍蜀。

translations.literal: The court heard of it and dispatched Shaanxi infantry, cavalry, arms, and equipment in an unbroken stream to garrison Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard of it, Shaanxi infantry, cavalry, arms, and equipment were sent in an unbroken stream to garrison Shu.

sentences.zh: 詔趣方平行，許以便宜從事，方平曰：「此必妄也。」

translations.literal: An edict urged Fangping to hurry; he was permitted discretionary authority. Fangping said: "This is certainly false."
translations.idiomatic: An edict urged Fangping to hurry, granting him discretionary authority. Fangping said, "This is certainly false."

sentences.zh: 道遇戍卒，皆遣歸，他役盡罷。

translations.literal: On the road he met garrison troops and sent them all back; all other levies were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met garrison troops and sent them all back; all other levies were stopped.

sentences.zh: 適上元張燈，城門三夕不閉，得邛部川譯人始造此語者，梟首境上，而流其餘黨，蜀人遂安。

translations.literal: It happened to be the Lantern Festival; lanterns were hung and the gates were left unclosed for three nights. He obtained the interpreter from Qiongbu who had first fabricated this tale, beheaded him on the border, and banished the rest of the faction, and the people of Shu were then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: It happened to be the Lantern Festival; lanterns were hung and the gates were left unclosed for three nights. He obtained the interpreter from Qiongbu who had first fabricated this tale, beheaded him on the border, and banished the rest of the faction, and the people of Shu were then at peace.

sentences.zh: 復以三司使召。

translations.literal: He was again summoned as commissioner of the Three Fiscal Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: He was again summoned as commissioner of the Three Fiscal Commissions.

sentences.zh: 方西鄙用兵，兩蜀多所調發，方平為奏免橫賦四十萬，減鑄鐵錢十餘萬緡。

translations.literal: As the western border was at war, the Two Shu were heavily levied; Fangping memorialized to remit forty thousand in irregular exactions and reduce iron coin casting by more than one hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: As the western border was at war, the Two Shu were heavily levied; Fangping memorialized to remit forty thousand in irregular exactions and reduce iron coin casting by more than one hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 又建言：「國家都陳留，當四通五達之道，非若雍、洛有山川足恃，特倚重兵以立國耳。

translations.literal: He also submitted advice: "The state capital is at Chenliu, situated on roads running in all four directions and five—unlike Yong and Luo, which have mountains and rivers sufficient to rely upon; it depends solely on heavy troops to uphold the state.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted advice: "The state capital is at Chenliu, on roads running in every direction—unlike Yong and Luo, which have mountains and rivers enough to rely on; it depends solely on heavy troops to uphold the state.

sentences.zh: 兵恃食，食恃漕運，以汴為主，汴帶引淮、江，利盡南海。

translations.literal: Troops rely on food, food relies on transport; the Bian Canal is primary—the Bian leads in the Huai and Yangtze, drawing the profit of the entire Southern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Troops rely on food, food relies on transport; the Bian Canal is primary—the Bian leads in the Huai and Yangtze and draws the profit of the entire southern sea.

sentences.zh: 天聖已前，歲調民浚之，故水行地中。

translations.literal: Before Tiansheng, the people were levied annually to dredge it, so the water ran within the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Before Tiansheng, the people were levied annually to dredge it, so the water ran within the earth.

sentences.zh: 其後，淺妄者爭以裁減役費為功，汴日以塞，今仰而望焉，是利尺寸而喪丘山也。」

translations.literal: Afterward shallow and reckless men competed to count cutting labor costs as merit; the Bian grew blocked day by day—now one looks up at it. This is profiting inches and losing hills."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward shallow and reckless men competed to count cutting labor costs as merit; the Bian grew blocked day by day—now one looks up at it. This is profiting inches and losing hills."

sentences.zh: 乃畫上十四策。

translations.literal: He thereupon presented a diagram with fourteen stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon presented a diagram with fourteen stratagems.

sentences.zh: 富弼讀其奏，漏盡十刻，帝稱善。

translations.literal: Fu Bi read his memorial until the tenth watch of the night was done; the emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi read his memorial until the tenth watch of the night was done; the emperor praised it.

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「此國計大本，非常奏也。」

translations.literal: Bi said: "This is the great foundation of national planning, not an ordinary memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "This is the great foundation of national planning, not an ordinary memorial."

sentences.zh: 悉如其說行之。

translations.literal: All was carried out according to his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: All was carried out according to his proposal.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞、知南京。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and made prefect of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and made prefect of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以工部尚書帥秦州。

translations.literal: Before long, as Minister of Works he commanded Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, as Minister of Works he took command of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 諜告夏人將壓境，方平料簡士馬，聲言出塞。

translations.literal: Spies reported that the Xia were about to press the border; Fangping inspected troops and horses and declared he would take the field beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported that the Xia were about to press the border; Fangping inspected troops and horses and declared he would take the field beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 已而寇不至，言者論其輕舉，曾公亮曰：「兵不出塞，何名輕舉？

translations.literal: When the raiders did not come, critics judged him rash. Zeng Gongliang said: "If troops do not go beyond the passes, how is that called rash?
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders did not come, critics judged him rash. Zeng Gongliang said, "If troops do not go beyond the passes, how is that called rash?

sentences.zh: 寇之不得至，有備故也。

translations.literal: That the enemy could not come was because there was preparation.
translations.idiomatic: That the enemy could not come was because there was preparation.

sentences.zh: 倘罪之，後之邊臣，將不敢為先事之備矣。」

translations.literal: If we punish him, frontier officials hereafter will not dare make preparations beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: If we punish him, frontier officials hereafter will not dare make preparations beforehand."

sentences.zh: 方平不自安，請知南京。

translations.literal: Fangping himself was uneasy and requested appointment as prefect of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping himself was uneasy and requested appointment as prefect of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，遷禮部尚書，請知鄆州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, Fangping was promoted to Minister of Rites and requested to be prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, he was promoted to Minister of Rites and requested to be prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，為學士承旨。

translations.literal: On his return he was made chief Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made chief Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，召至福寧殿，帝馮几言，言不可辨。

translations.literal: The emperor was unwell and summoned him to the Hall of Blessings and Tranquility; leaning on the armrest the emperor spoke, but his words could not be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was unwell and summoned him to the Hall of Blessings and Tranquility; leaning on the armrest the emperor spoke, but his words could not be distinguished.

sentences.zh: 方平進筆請，乃書云：「明日降詔，立皇太子。」

translations.literal: Fangping presented a brush and requested; the emperor then wrote: "Tomorrow issue an edict to establish the heir apparent."
translations.idiomatic: Fangping presented a brush and requested; the emperor then wrote, "Tomorrow issue an edict to establish the heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 方平抗聲曰：「必潁王也，嫡長而賢，請書其名。」

translations.literal: Fangping said in a firm voice: "It must be the Prince of Ying—eldest legitimate son and worthy; please write his name."
translations.idiomatic: Fangping said in a firm voice, "It must be the Prince of Ying—eldest legitimate son and worthy; please write his name."

sentences.zh: 帝力疾書之，乃退草制。

translations.literal: The emperor, straining against illness, wrote it, and Fangping then withdrew to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, straining against illness, wrote it, and Fangping then withdrew to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，召見，請約山陵費，帝曰：「奉先可損乎？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Fangping was summoned and asked to limit tomb expenses. The emperor said: "Can what is done for the ancestors be reduced?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, he was summoned and asked to limit tomb expenses. The emperor said, "Can what is done for the ancestors be reduced?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「遺制固云，以先志行之，可謂孝矣。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The testamentary instructions indeed say so—to carry out the former emperor's intent may be called filial."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The testamentary instructions indeed say so—to carry out the former emperor's intent may be called filial."

sentences.zh: 又請差減錫賚，以乾興為準，費省什七八。

translations.literal: He also requested reducing bestowals on the model of the Qianxing era, saving seven or eight tenths of the expense.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested reducing bestowals on the model of the Qianxing era, saving seven or eight tenths of the expense.

sentences.zh: 方平進詔草，帝親批之，曰：「卿文章典雅，煥然有三代風，又善以豐為約，意博而辭寡，雖《書》之訓誥，殆無加也。」

translations.literal: Fangping submitted a draft edict; the emperor personally annotated it, saying: "Your writing is refined and elegant, radiant with the style of the Three Dynasties; you are also skilled at making abundance concise—thought broad yet language spare. Even the admonitions of the Documents can scarcely surpass it."
translations.idiomatic: Fangping submitted a draft edict; the emperor personally annotated it, saying, "Your writing is refined and elegant, radiant with the style of the Three Dynasties; you are also skilled at making abundance concise—thought broad yet language spare. Even the admonitions of the Documents can scarcely surpass it."

sentences.zh: 其見稱重如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus was he esteemed.

sentences.zh: 拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞司馬光疏其不當用，不聽。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Sima Guang memorialized that he should not be appointed; the emperor did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Sima Guang memorialized that he should not be appointed; the emperor did not heed it.

sentences.zh: 光解中丞，曾公亮議用王安石，方平以為不可。

translations.literal: Guang resigned as censor-in-chief; Zeng Gongliang proposed employing Wang Anshi; Fangping thought this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Guang resigned as censor-in-chief; Zeng Gongliang proposed employing Wang Anshi; Fangping thought this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 數日，遭父憂，服闋，以觀文殿學士留守西京。

translations.literal: Within days he suffered his father's death; when mourning ended he was made academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and left to guard the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he suffered his father's death; when mourning ended he was made academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and left to guard the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 入覲，留判尚書都省，力請知陳州。

translations.literal: On entering audience he was retained to direct the general office of the Ministry Secretariat, but strongly requested to be prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On entering audience he was retained to direct the general office of the Ministry Secretariat, but strongly requested to be prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 安石行新法，方平陛辭，極論其害，曰：「民猶水也，可以載舟，亦可以覆舟；

translations.literal: When Anshi implemented the New Policies, Fangping took leave at court and argued vehemently against their harm, saying: "The people are like water—they can bear the boat, and they can overturn it;
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi implemented the New Policies, Fangping took leave at court and argued vehemently against their harm, saying, "The people are like water—they can bear the boat, and they can overturn it;

sentences.zh: 兵猶火也，弗戢必自焚。

translations.literal: Armies are like fire; if not restrained they will surely burn themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Armies are like fire; if not restrained they will surely burn themselves.

sentences.zh: 若新法卒行，必有覆舟、自焚之禍。」

translations.literal: If the New Policies are finally carried out, there will surely be the calamities of overturning the boat and self-immolation."
translations.idiomatic: If the New Policies are finally carried through, there will surely be the calamities of capsizing the boat and burning oneself.

sentences.zh: 帝憮然。

translations.literal: The emperor looked troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked troubled.

sentences.zh: 韓絳主西師，慶卒亂，京西轉運使令一路各會兵於州，民大駭。

translations.literal: Han Jiang directed the western campaign; Qingzhou troops mutinied, and the transport commissioner of western Jingdong ordered each circuit to assemble troops at the prefectures, greatly alarming the people.
translations.idiomatic: While Han Jiang directed the western campaign, Qingzhou troops mutinied, and the transport commissioner of western Jingdong ordered each circuit to assemble troops at the prefectures, throwing the people into great alarm.

sentences.zh: 方平持檄不下而奏之，帝曰：「守臣不當爾邪！」

translations.literal: Fangping held the dispatch and did not issue it, memorializing instead. The emperor said: "Should not a guardian official act thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Fangping held the dispatch and did not issue it, memorializing instead. The emperor said, "Should not a guardian official act thus!"

sentences.zh: 命罷諸郡兵。

translations.literal: He ordered the troops of all prefectures disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the troops of all prefectures disbanded.

sentences.zh: 召為宣徽北院使，留京師。

translations.literal: He was summoned as commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Military Affairs Commission and kept at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Military Affairs Commission and kept at the capital.

sentences.zh: 王安石深沮之，以為青州。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi strongly obstructed him and had him made prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi strongly obstructed him and had him appointed prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，帝問祖宗御戎之要，對曰：「太祖不勤遠略，如靈夏、河西，皆因其酋豪，許之世襲；

translations.literal: Before he departed, the emperor asked the essentials of the founding ancestors' control of the barbarians. He replied: "Taizu did not strive for distant campaigns; in Lingxia, Hexi, and the like, he relied on their tribal chiefs and allowed them hereditary succession;
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed, the emperor asked the essentials of the founding ancestors' control of the barbarians. He replied, "Taizu did not strive for distant campaigns; in Lingxia, Hexi, and the like, he relied on their tribal chiefs and allowed them hereditary succession;

sentences.zh: 環州董遵誨、西山郭進、關南李漢超，皆優其祿賜，寬其文法。

translations.literal: Dong Zunhui of Huanzhou, Guo Jin of Xishan, and Li Hanchao of Guannan were all given generous salaries and rewards, and their legal burdens were eased.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zunhui of Huanzhou, Guo Jin of Xishan, and Li Hanchao of Guannan were all given generous salaries and rewards, and their legal burdens were eased.

sentences.zh: 諸將財力豐而威令行，間諜精審，吏士用命，故能以十五萬人而獲百萬之用。

translations.literal: The generals were rich in resources and their commands effective; spies were precise and thorough; officers and soldiers obeyed orders—thus with one hundred fifty thousand men they obtained the use of a million.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were rich in resources and their commands effective; spies were precise and thorough; officers and soldiers obeyed orders—thus with one hundred fifty thousand men they obtained the use of a million.

sentences.zh: 及太宗謀取燕薊，又內徙李彝興、馮暉，於是朝廷始旰食矣。

translations.literal: When Taizong schemed to take Yan and Ji and moreover moved Li Yixing and Feng Hui inward, the court then began to eat late in worry.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong schemed to take Yan and Ji and moreover moved Li Yixing and Feng Hui inward, the court then began to lose its ease.

sentences.zh: 真宗澶淵之克，與契丹盟，至今人不識兵革。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong prevailed at Chanyuan and made alliance with the Khitan, to this day people do not know arms and armor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong prevailed at Chanyuan and made alliance with the Khitan, to this day people scarcely know war.

sentences.zh: 三朝之事如此。

translations.literal: The affairs of the three reigns were thus.
translations.idiomatic: The affairs of the three reigns were thus.

sentences.zh: 近歲疆塲之臣，乃欲試天下於一擲，事成徼利，不成詒患，不可聽也。」

translations.literal: In recent years frontier officials wish to stake the empire on a single throw—if it succeeds they seek profit, if it fails they bequeath disaster. This must not be heeded."
translations.idiomatic: In recent years frontier officials wish to stake the empire on a single throw—if it succeeds they seek profit, if it fails they bequeath disaster. This must not be heeded.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「慶曆以來，卿知之乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Since the Qingli era, do you know it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Since the Qingli era, do you know it?

sentences.zh: 元昊初臣，何以待之？」

translations.literal: When Yuanhao first submitted, how was he treated?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao first submitted, how was he treated?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣時為學士，誓詔封冊，皆出臣手。」

translations.literal: He replied: "At the time I was an academician; the oath edicts and investiture documents all came from my hand."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "At the time I was an academician; the oath edicts and investiture documents all came from my hand."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿時已為學士，可謂舊德矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "At the time you were already an academician—you may be called an elder of merit."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "At the time you were already an academician—you may be called an elder of merit."

sentences.zh: 契丹泛使蕭禧來議疆事，臨當辭，臥驛中不起。

translations.literal: The Khitan general envoy Xiao Xi came to discuss border affairs; when about to take leave he lay in the post station and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan general envoy Xiao Xi came to discuss border affairs; when about to take leave he lay in the post station and would not rise.

sentences.zh: 方平謂樞密使吳充曰：「但令主者日致饋勿問，且使邊郡檄其國可也。」

translations.literal: Fangping said to Military Affairs Commissioner Wu Chong: "Simply have the host send provisions daily without inquiry, and moreover have the border prefectures dispatch a note to their state—that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Fangping said to Military Affairs Commissioner Wu Chong, "Simply have the host send provisions daily without inquiry, and moreover have the border prefectures dispatch a note to their state—that will suffice."

sentences.zh: 充啟從之，禧即行。

translations.literal: Chong reported and followed this; Xi then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Chong reported and followed this; Xi then departed.

sentences.zh: 除中太一宮使。

translations.literal: He was appointed commissioner of the Central Supreme Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commissioner of the Central Supreme Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 王安石弛銅禁，奸民日銷錢為器，邊關海舶不復譏錢出，錢日耗。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi relaxed the copper prohibition; scoundrels daily melted coin into vessels; border passes and sea ships no longer inspected coin leaving; coin was daily depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi relaxed the copper prohibition; scoundrels daily melted coin into vessels; border passes and sea ships no longer inspected coin leaving; coin was daily depleted.

sentences.zh: 方平極論其害，請詰安石：「舉累朝之令典，一旦削除之，其意安在？」

translations.literal: Fangping argued vehemently against its harm and requested that Anshi be questioned: "The canonical statutes of successive reigns—why abolish them all at once? What is the intent?"
translations.idiomatic: Fangping argued vehemently against its harm and requested that Anshi be questioned: "The canonical statutes of successive reigns—why abolish them all at once? What is the intent?"

sentences.zh: 帝頗採其言，而方平求去。

translations.literal: The emperor largely adopted his words, but Fangping requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely adopted his words, but Fangping requested to leave office.

sentences.zh: 進使南院，判應天府。

translations.literal: He was advanced as commissioner of the Southern Bureau and concurrently directed Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced as commissioner of the Southern Bureau and concurrently directed Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕欲卿與韓絳共事，而卿論政不同；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I wished you to serve together with Han Jiang, yet your views on government differ;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I wished you to serve together with Han Jiang, yet your views on government differ;

sentences.zh: 欲置卿樞密，而卿論兵復異。

translations.literal: I wished to place you in the Military Affairs Commission, yet your views on war again differ.
translations.idiomatic: I wished to place you in the Military Affairs Commission, yet your views on war again differ.

sentences.zh: 卿受先帝末命，訖無以副朕意乎？」

translations.literal: You received the late emperor's final charge—can you in the end not fulfill my intent?"
translations.idiomatic: You received the late emperor's final charge—can you in the end not fulfill my intent?

sentences.zh: 遂行。

translations.literal: He then departed.
translations.idiomatic: He then departed.

sentences.zh: 高麗使過府，長吏當送迎，方平言：「臣班視二府，不可為陪臣屈。」

translations.literal: When a Goryeo envoy passed through the prefecture, the chief official was to escort him. Fangping said: "My rank is equal to the two councils; I cannot bow to a tributary envoy."
translations.idiomatic: When a Goryeo envoy passed through the prefecture, the chief official was to escort him. Fangping said, "My rank is equal to the two councils; I cannot bow to a tributary envoy."

sentences.zh: 詔但遣少尹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered only the vice-prefect sent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered only the vice-prefect sent.

sentences.zh: 王師征安南，方平言：「舉西北壯士健馬，棄之炎荒，其患有不可勝言者。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Annan, Fangping said: "To raise stalwart men and strong horses from the northwest and abandon them in the burning wilds—the calamities are beyond telling.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army campaigned against Annan, Fangping said, "To raise stalwart men and strong horses from the northwest and abandon them in the burning wilds—the calamities are beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 若師老費財，無功而還，社稷之福也。」

translations.literal: If the army grows weary, expenses mount, and it returns without achievement—that would be the fortune of the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: If the army grows weary, expenses mount, and it returns without achievement—that would be the fortune of the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 後皆如其言。

translations.literal: Afterward all came to pass as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward all came to pass as he had said.

sentences.zh: 方平慷慨有氣節，既告老，論事益切，至於用兵、起獄，尤反覆言之。

translations.literal: Fangping was generous and possessed integrity; after retiring he spoke on affairs with growing urgency, and on employing troops and initiating prosecutions he spoke with especial repetition.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping was generous and possessed integrity; after retiring he spoke on affairs with growing urgency, and on employing troops and initiating prosecutions he spoke with especial repetition.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「臣且死，見先帝地下，有以藉口矣。」

translations.literal: He also said: "When I am about to die and meet the late emperor underground, I shall have words to answer with."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When I am about to die and meet the late emperor underground, I shall have words to answer with."

sentences.zh: 平居未嘗以言徇物、以色假人。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he never bent his words to please others or lent his countenance to deceive people.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary life he never bent his words to please others or lent his countenance to deceive people.

sentences.zh: 守蜀日，得眉山蘇洵與其二子軾、轍，深器異之。

translations.literal: While governing Shu he obtained Su Xun of Meishan and his two sons Shi and Zhe, and deeply admired them as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Shu he obtained Su Xun of Meishan and his two sons Shi and Zhe, and deeply admired them as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 嘗薦軾為諫官。

translations.literal: He once recommended Shi as remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: He once recommended Shi as remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 軾下制獄，又抗章為請，故軾終身敬事之，敘其文，以比孔融、諸葛亮。

translations.literal: When Shi was sent to the drafting prison, Fangping again submitted a memorial in his defense; therefore Shi revered him all his life and wrote of his writings, comparing him to Kong Rong and Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi was sent to the drafting prison, Fangping again submitted a memorial in his defense; therefore Shi revered him all his life and wrote of his writings, comparing him to Kong Rong and Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 晚受知神宗。

translations.literal: In his later years he won Shenzong's trust.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he won Shenzong's trust.

sentences.zh: 王安石方用事，嶷然不小屈，以是望高一時。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi was in power he stood erect and would not yield slightly; on this account his reputation towered for a time.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi was in power he stood erect and would not yield slightly; on this account his reputation towered for a time.

sentences.zh: 守宋都日，富弼自亳移汝，過見之曰：「人固難知也。」

translations.literal: While guarding the Song capital, Fu Bi moved from Bo to Ru and, passing through, visited him and said: "People are indeed hard to know."
translations.idiomatic: While guarding the Song capital, Fu Bi moved from Bo to Ru and, passing through, visited him and said, "People are indeed hard to know."

sentences.zh: 方平曰：「謂王安石乎？

translations.literal: Fangping said: "You mean Wang Anshi?
translations.idiomatic: Fangping said, "You mean Wang Anshi?

sentences.zh: 亦豈難知者！

translations.literal: He is hardly hard to know!
translations.idiomatic: He is hardly hard to know!

sentences.zh: 方平頃知皇祐貢舉，或稱其文學，辟以考校。

translations.literal: Fangping had lately directed the Huangyou civil examination; some praised Anshi's literary learning, and Fangping recruited him for examination duty.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping had lately directed the Huangyou civil examination; some praised Anshi's literary learning, and Fangping recruited him for examination duty.

sentences.zh: 既入院，凡院中之事，皆欲紛更。

translations.literal: Once he entered the academy, he wished to overturn everything in the institution.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered the academy, he wished to overturn everything in the institution.

sentences.zh: 方平惡其人，檄使出，自是未嘗與語也。」

translations.literal: Fangping detested the man and dispatched him out by order; from then on he never spoke with him."
translations.idiomatic: Fangping detested the man and dispatched him out by order; from then on he never spoke with him."

sentences.zh: 弼有愧色，蓋弼素亦善安石云。

translations.literal: Bi showed a look of shame—for Bi had also been friendly with Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Bi showed a look of shame—for Bi had also been friendly with Anshi.

sentences.zh: 王拱辰

translations.literal: Wang Gongchen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gongchen

sentences.zh: 王拱辰，字君貺，開封咸平人。

translations.literal: Wang Gongchen, courtesy name Junkuang, was a native of Xianping in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gongchen, styled Junkuang, was from Xianping in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 元名拱壽，年十九，舉進士第一，仁宗賜以今名。

translations.literal: His original name was Gongshou. At nineteen he took first place in the jinshi examination, and Renzong bestowed his present name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Gongshou. At nineteen he took first place in the jinshi examination, and Renzong bestowed his present name.

sentences.zh: 通判懷州，入直集賢院，歷鹽鐵判官、修起居注、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was deputy prefect of Huaizhou, entered direct service in the Academy of Worthies, and served in turn as salt and iron judge, compiler of the Daily Records, and drafting edict-er.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice-prefect of Huaizhou, entered direct service in the Academy of Worthies, and served in turn as salt and iron judge, compiler of the Daily Records, and drafting edict-er.

sentences.zh: 慶曆元年，為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingli he became Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingli he became Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 契丹使劉六符嘗謂賈昌朝曰：「塘濼何為者？

translations.literal: The Khitan envoy Liu Liufu once said to Jia Changchao: "What are these ponds and marshes for?
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan envoy Liu Liufu once said to Jia Changchao, "What are these ponds and marshes for?

sentences.zh: 一葦可杭，投箠可平；

translations.literal: A single reed can ferry across; throw a staff and they can be leveled;
translations.idiomatic: A single reed can ferry across; throw a staff and they can be leveled;

sentences.zh: 不然，決其堤，十萬土囊，即可路矣。」

translations.literal: otherwise breach the dikes—with one hundred thousand earth bags you can make a road at once."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise breach the dikes—with one hundred thousand earth bags you can make a road at once."

sentences.zh: 仁宗以問拱辰，對曰：「兵事尚詭，彼誠有謀，不應以語我，此誇言爾。

translations.literal: Renzong asked Gongchen, who replied: "Military affairs value deception; if they truly had a plan they would not tell us—this is mere boasting.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong asked Gongchen, who replied, "Military affairs value deception; if they truly had a plan they would not tell us—this is mere boasting.

sentences.zh: 設險守國，先王不廢，而祖宗所以限敵人也。」

translations.literal: Establishing defenses to guard the state—the former kings did not abolish this, and it is how the ancestors restrained the foe."
translations.idiomatic: Establishing defenses to guard the state—the former kings did not abolish this, and it is how the ancestors restrained the foe."

sentences.zh: 至是，又使六符來，求關南十縣，斥太宗伐燕為無名，舉朝莫知所答。

translations.literal: At this time Liufu was again sent, demanding the ten counties south of the pass and denouncing Taizong's campaign against Yan as without cause; the whole court knew not how to answer.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Liufu was again sent, demanding the ten counties south of the pass and denouncing Taizong's campaign against Yan as without cause; the whole court knew not how to answer.

sentences.zh: 拱辰曰：「王師征河東，契丹既通使，而寇石嶺關以援賊。

translations.literal: Gongchen said: "When the imperial army campaigned in Hedong, the Khitan had already sent envoys, yet they raided Shiling Pass to aid the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchen said, "When the imperial army campaigned in Hedong, the Khitan had already sent envoys, yet they raided Shiling Pass to aid the rebels.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，遂回軍伐之，豈謂無名？」

translations.literal: Taizong was enraged and turned the army to attack them—how can this be called without cause?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was enraged and turned the army to attack them—how can this be called without cause?"

sentences.zh: 乃作報書曰：「既交石嶺之鋒，遂有薊門之役。」

translations.literal: He then composed a reply stating: "Once blades crossed at Shiling, there followed the campaign at Jimen."
translations.idiomatic: He then composed a reply stating, "Once blades crossed at Shiling, there followed the campaign at Jimen."

sentences.zh: 契丹得報，遂繼好如初。

translations.literal: The Khitan received the reply and renewed amity as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan received the reply and renewed amity as before.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，謂輔臣曰：「非拱辰深練故實，殆難答也。」

translations.literal: The emperor rejoiced and told the chief ministers: "Had not Gongchen been deeply versed in past facts, it would have been hard to answer."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejoiced and told the chief ministers, "Had not Gongchen been deeply versed in past facts, it would have been hard to answer."

sentences.zh: 權知開封府，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was acting prefect of Kaifeng and appointed censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was acting prefect of Kaifeng and appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 夏竦除樞密使，拱辰言：「竦經略西師，無功稱而歸。

translations.literal: Xia Song was appointed commissioner of military affairs. Gongchen said: "Song directed the western campaign and returned claiming no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song was appointed commissioner of military affairs. Gongchen said, "Song directed the western campaign and returned claiming no achievement.

sentences.zh: 今置諸二府，何以厲世？」

translations.literal: Now to place him in the two councils—how can this admonish the age?"
translations.idiomatic: Now to place him in the two councils—how can this admonish the age?"

sentences.zh: 因對，極論之。

translations.literal: At audience he argued the point to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he argued the point to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 帝未省，遽起，拱辰前引裾，乃納其說，竦遂罷。

translations.literal: The emperor did not understand and rose abruptly; Gongchen went forward and seized his robe, and only then was his argument accepted; Song was then removed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not understand and rose abruptly; Gongchen went forward and seized his robe, and only then was his argument accepted; Song was then removed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「滕宗諒在慶州，所為不度，而但降秩守虢，懼邊臣則效，宜施重責。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Teng Zongliang in Qing Prefecture acted without measure, yet was only demoted in rank to guard Guo—fearing frontier officials will imitate him, heavy punishment should be applied."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Teng Zongliang in Qing Prefecture acted without measure, yet was only demoted in rank to guard Guo—fearing frontier officials will imitate him, heavy punishment should be applied."

sentences.zh: 未聽，即家居，求自貶。

translations.literal: Not heeded, he immediately retired at home and requested self-demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Not heeded, he immediately retired at home and requested self-demotion.

sentences.zh: 乃徙宗諒岳州，敕拱辰赴臺。

translations.literal: Zongliang was then transferred to Yue Prefecture, and Gongchen was ordered to return to the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Zongliang was then transferred to Yue Prefecture, and Gongchen was ordered to return to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 入見，帝曰：「言事官第自舉職，勿以朝廷未行為沮己，而輕去以沽名。

translations.literal: On entering audience the emperor said: "Remonstrance officials should simply perform their duties; do not, because the court has not acted, discourage yourselves and lightly leave to seek a name.
translations.idiomatic: On entering audience the emperor said, "Remonstrance officials should simply perform their duties; do not, because the court has not acted, discourage yourselves and lightly leave to seek a name.

sentences.zh: 自今有當言者，宜力陳毋避。」

translations.literal: From now on, when there is something that should be said, you should state it forcefully without evasion."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, when there is something that should be said, you should state it forcefully without evasion."

sentences.zh: 僧紹宗以鑄佛像惑眾，都人競投金冶中，宮掖亦出貲佐之。

translations.literal: The monk Shaozong deluded the masses by casting a Buddha image; the capital's people competed to cast gold into the furnace, and the palace also contributed funds to assist.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Shaozong deluded the masses by casting a Buddha image; the capital's people competed to cast gold into the furnace, and the palace also contributed funds to assist.

sentences.zh: 拱辰言：「西師宿邊，而財費於不急，動士心，起民怨。」

translations.literal: Gongchen said: "The western campaign camps on the frontier, yet wealth is spent on what is not urgent—this stirs soldiers' hearts and raises the people's resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Gongchen said, "The western campaign camps on the frontier, yet wealth is spent on what is not urgent—this stirs soldiers' hearts and raises the people's resentment."

sentences.zh: 詔亟禁之。

translations.literal: An edict urgently forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict urgently forbade it.

sentences.zh: 蘇舜欽會賓客於進奏院，王益柔醉作《傲歌》，拱辰風其僚魚周詢、劉元瑜舉劾之。

translations.literal: Su Shunqin entertained guests at the Memorial Transmission Court; Wang Yirou, drunk, composed the "Song of Arrogance." Gongchen prompted his colleagues Yu Zhouxun and Liu Yuanyu to impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shunqin entertained guests at the Memorial Transmission Court; Wang Yirou, drunk, composed the Song of Arrogance. Gongchen prompted his colleagues Yu Zhouxun and Liu Yuanyu to impeach them.

sentences.zh: 兩人既竄廢，同席者俱逐。

translations.literal: Once the two were banished and dismissed, all who shared the table were expelled as well.
translations.idiomatic: Once the two were banished and dismissed, all who shared the table were expelled as well.

sentences.zh: 時杜衍、范仲淹為政，多所更張，拱辰之黨不便。

translations.literal: At the time Du Yan and Fan Zhongyan held power and made many changes; Gongchen's faction found this inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Du Yan and Fan Zhongyan held power and made many changes; Gongchen's faction found this inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 舜欽、益柔皆仲淹所薦，而舜欽，衍婿也，故因是傾之，由此為公議所薄。

translations.literal: Shunqin and Yirou were both recommended by Zhongyan, and Shunqin was Yan's son-in-law; therefore he used this to overthrow them, and on this account was slighted in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Shunqin and Yirou were both recommended by Zhongyan, and Shunqin was Yan's son-in-law; therefore he used this to overthrow them, and on this account was slighted in public opinion.

sentences.zh: 復以翰林學士權三司使。

translations.literal: He again served as Hanlin academician and acting commissioner of the Three Fiscal Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Hanlin academician and acting commissioner of the Three Fiscal Commissions.

sentences.zh: 坐舉富民鄭旭，出知鄭州，徙澶、瀛、幷三州。

translations.literal: Because he had recommended the wealthy man Zheng Xu, he was sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou and transferred through the three prefectures of Chan, Ying, and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had recommended the wealthy man Zheng Xu, he was sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou and transferred through the three prefectures of Chan, Ying, and Bing.

sentences.zh: 數歲還，為學士承旨兼侍讀。

translations.literal: After several years he returned and was made chief Hanlin academician and lecturer-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he returned and was made chief Hanlin academician and lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 帝於邇英閣置《太玄經》、蓍草，顧曰：「朕每閱此。

translations.literal: The emperor placed the Classic of the Supreme Mystery and yarrow stalks in the Hall of Near Excellence and, turning, said: "I often peruse these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor placed the Classic of the Supreme Mystery and yarrow stalks in the Hall of Near Excellence and, turning, said, "I often peruse these.

sentences.zh: 卿亦知其說乎？」

translations.literal: Do you also know its doctrine?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you also know its doctrine?"

sentences.zh: 拱辰具以對，且曰：「願陛下垂意《六經》，旁採史策，此不足學也。」

translations.literal: Gongchen answered in full detail and moreover said: "I hope Your Majesty will fix your mind on the Six Classics and gather broadly from historical records—this is not worth studying."
translations.idiomatic: Gongchen answered in full detail and moreover said, "I hope Your Majesty will fix your mind on the Six Classics and gather broadly from historical records—this is not worth studying."

sentences.zh: 至和三年，復拜三司使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhihe he was again appointed commissioner of the Three Fiscal Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhihe he was again appointed commissioner of the Three Fiscal Commissions.

sentences.zh: 聘契丹，見其主混同江，設宴垂釣，每得魚，必酌拱辰酒，親鼓琵琶以侑飲。

translations.literal: As envoy to the Khitan he met their sovereign at the Hun Tong River; a banquet was set and they fished; whenever a fish was caught he would pour wine for Gongchen and personally play the pipa to accompany the drinking.
translations.idiomatic: As envoy to the Khitan he met their sovereign at the Hun Tong River; a banquet was set and they fished; whenever a fish was caught he would pour wine for Gongchen and personally play the pipa to accompany the drinking.

sentences.zh: 謂其相曰：「此南朝少年狀元也，入翰林十五年，故吾厚待之。」

translations.literal: He said to his chief minister: "This is the southern court's young zhuangyuan; he has been in the Hanlin for fifteen years—therefore I treat him generously."
translations.idiomatic: He said to his chief minister, "This is the southern court's young zhuangyuan; he has been in the Hanlin for fifteen years—therefore I treat him generously."

sentences.zh: 使還，御史趙抃論其輒當非正之禮，「異時北使援此以請，將何辭拒之？」

translations.literal: On returning from the mission, Censor Zhao Bian criticized his readily accepting improper rites: "If in future northern envoys cite this in request, with what words will we refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: On returning from the mission, Censor Zhao Bian criticized his readily accepting improper rites: "If in future northern envoys cite this in request, with what words will we refuse?"

sentences.zh: 湖南轉運判官李章、知潭州任顓市死商真珠，事敗，具獄上，拱辰悉入珠掖庭。

translations.literal: Li Zhang, transport judge of Hunan, and Ren Yan, prefect of Tanzhou, purchased pearls from a dead merchant; when the affair was exposed the full case was submitted, and Gongchen sent all the pearls to the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhang, transport judge of Hunan, and Ren Yan, prefect of Tanzhou, purchased pearls from a dead merchant; when the affair was exposed the full case was submitted, and Gongchen sent all the pearls to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 抃並劾之。

translations.literal: Bian impeached him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Bian impeached him as well.

sentences.zh: 除宣徽北院使，抃言：「宣徽之職，本以待勛勞者，唯前執政及節度使得為之，拱辰安得污此選？」

translations.literal: He was appointed commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Military Affairs Commission. Bian said: "The post of Palace Military Affairs Commissioner was originally for those awaiting merit and toil; only former chief administrators and military commissioners may hold it—how can Gongchen stain this appointment?"
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Military Affairs Commission. Bian said, "The post of Palace Military Affairs Commissioner was originally for those awaiting merit and toil; only former chief administrators and military commissioners may hold it—how can Gongchen stain this appointment?"

sentences.zh: 乃以端明殿學士知永興軍，歷泰、定二州、河南大名府，積官至吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was then made academician of the Duanming Hall and prefect of Yongxing Army, served in turn the two prefectures of Tai and Ding and Henan's Daming Prefecture, and rose by accumulated offices to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made academician of the Duanming Hall and prefect of Yongxing Army, served in turn the two prefectures of Tai and Ding and Henan's Daming Prefecture, and rose by accumulated offices to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 神宗登極，恩當轉僕射，歐陽脩以為此宰相官，不應序進，但遷太子少保。

translations.literal: When Shenzong acceded, by grace he should have been transferred to Vice Director; Ouyang Xiu held that this was a chief minister's office and should not be advanced in sequence, and he was only promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong acceded, by grace he should have been transferred to Vice Director; Ouyang Xiu held that this was a chief minister's office and should not be advanced in sequence, and he was only promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，復以北院使召還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining he was again summoned back as commissioner of the Northern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xining he was again summoned back as commissioner of the Northern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 王安石參知政事，惡其異己，乘二相有故，出為應天府。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi became Vice Grand Councilor he hated those who differed from him; seizing an occasion when the two chief ministers had business, he had Gongchen sent out as prefect of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi became Vice Grand Councilor he hated those who differed from him; seizing an occasion when the two chief ministers had business, he had Gongchen sent out as prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 八年，入朝，為中太一宮使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered court and was made Commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he returned to court and was appointed Commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，轉南院使，賜金方團帶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanfeng era he was transferred to Commissioner of the Southern Academy and granted a gold square belt with ornamental plaques.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanfeng period he was moved to Commissioner of the Southern Academy and awarded a gold square belt with ornamental plaques.

sentences.zh: 再判大名，改武安軍節度使。

translations.literal: Again he served as administrative commissioner of Daming and was changed to Military Commissioner of the Wu'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: He again administered Daming and was reassigned as Military Commissioner of the Wu'an Army.

sentences.zh: 三路籍民為保甲，日聚而教之，禁令苛急，往往去為盜，郡縣不敢以聞。

translations.literal: In the three circuits the people were registered into the baojia system, gathered daily for instruction; the prohibitions were harsh and urgent, and many often fled to become bandits, yet prefectures and counties dared not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Across the three circuits commoners were enrolled in the baojia system and assembled each day for drill; regulations were severe, and many fled into banditry, though local officials did not dare report it.

sentences.zh: 拱辰抗言其害曰：「非止困其財力，奪其農時，是以法驅之，使陷於罪罟也。

translations.literal: Gongchen vigorously spoke against its harm, saying: "It not only exhausts their financial strength and robs them of farming time—it uses the law to drive them and makes them fall into the net of crime.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchen forcefully protested the harm, declaring: "This does more than drain their resources and steal their farming season—it drives them by law straight into the snares of punishment.

sentences.zh: 浸淫為大盜，其兆已見。

translations.literal: Gradually spreading to become major bandits—the signs are already visible.
translations.idiomatic: Given time they will swell into large outlaw bands; the warning signs are already plain.

sentences.zh: 縱未能盡罷，願財損下戶以紓之。」

translations.literal: Even if it cannot be entirely abolished, I wish that the financial burden on lower-grade households be reduced to ease it."
translations.idiomatic: If the system cannot be wholly repealed, at least lighten the levy on the poorest households to give them relief."

sentences.zh: 主者指拱辰為沮法，拱辰曰：「此老臣所以報國也。」

translations.literal: The person in charge accused Gongchen of obstructing the law. Gongchen said: "This is how this old minister repays the state."
translations.idiomatic: Those in charge charged Gongchen with sabotaging the law. He replied: "This is precisely how an old servant serves his country."

sentences.zh: 上章不已。

translations.literal: He submitted memorial after memorial without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: He kept submitting memorials without letup.

sentences.zh: 帝悟，於是第五等戶得免。

translations.literal: The Emperor understood, and so fifth-grade households were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his point, and fifth-grade households were granted exemption.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，徙節彰德，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Gongchen was transferred to military command at Zhangde and given the honorary title of Grand Preceptor with the checker's prefix.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhezong came to the throne, he was reassigned to command at Zhangde and promoted to Honorary Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 是年薨，年七十四。

translations.literal: That same year he died, at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same year, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，諡懿恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Three Excellencies with Grand Prefecture honors, and given the posthumous name Yike.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was awarded Grand Prefecture honors equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous name Yike.

sentences.zh: 論曰：方平、拱辰之才，皆較然有過人者，而不免司馬光、趙抃之論。

translations.literal: The discussion says: The talents of Fangping and Gongchen both clearly surpassed others, yet they could not escape the criticisms of Sima Guang and Zhao Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe that Fangping and Gongchen were plainly men of exceptional ability, yet they still drew reproach from Sima Guang and Zhao Bian.

sentences.zh: 豈其英發之氣，勇於見得，一時趨鄉未能盡適於正與？

translations.literal: Was it perhaps that their spirited brilliance and boldness in advocating their views led them for a time to follow trends that did not entirely accord with what was right?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps their keen brilliance and eagerness to press their convictions led them, for a season, to follow fashions that were not wholly upright.

sentences.zh: 及新法行，方平痛陳其弊，拱辰爭保甲，言尤剴切，皆諤諤不少貶，為國老成，望始重矣。

translations.literal: When the New Policies were implemented, Fangping bitterly set forth their evils and Gongchen contested the baojia system with especially incisive words; all spoke frankly without much self-diminishment, and as elder statesmen serving the state their reputations were finally greatly esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the New Policies took effect, Fangping laid out their abuses with anguish and Gongchen fought the baojia system in language especially sharp; both remonstrated without trimming their words, and as seasoned servants of the realm they at last won great respect.

sentences.zh: 若方平識王安石於辟校貢舉之時，而知其後必亂政，其先見之明，無忝呂誨云。

translations.literal: As for Fangping's recognizing Wang Anshi when supervising the examination for graduates and knowing that he would later throw the government into disorder—his foresight did not fall short of what Lü Hui said.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping had spotted Wang Anshi during the provincial examination and foreseen that he would one day wreck the government—a prescience worthy of Lü Hui's praise.

sentences.zh: 張昪，字杲卿，韓城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Bian, courtesy name Gaoging, was a native of Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bian, styled Gaoging, came from Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為楚邱主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as chief clerk of Chuqiu.
translations.idiomatic: After taking the jinshi degree he became chief clerk of Chuqiu.

sentences.zh: 南京留守王曾稱其有公輔器。

translations.literal: Wang Zeng, Pacification Commissioner of the Southern Capital, said he had the makings of a high minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zeng, the Southern Capital pacification commissioner, declared that he possessed the caliber of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 累官度支員外郎。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached Vice Director of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: By successive appointments he rose to Vice Director of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 夏竦經略陝西，薦其才，換六宅使、涇原秦鳳安撫都監。

translations.literal: When Xia Song was Commissioner for Shaanxi he recommended Bian's talent; Bian was transferred to Six Mansions Commissioner and Pacification Superintendent for Jingyuan and Qinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song, while commissioner for Shaanxi, commended his ability, and Bian was reassigned as Six Mansions Commissioner and pacification superintendent for Jingyuan and Qinfeng.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以母老，求歸故官，得知絳州，改京西轉運使。

translations.literal: Before long, because his mother was elderly, he requested to return to his former rank; he was appointed prefect of Jiangzhou, then transferred to Transport Commissioner for the West Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, citing his mother's age, he asked to resume civil office; he was made prefect of Jiangzhou, then transport commissioner for the West Capital Circuit.

sentences.zh: 知鄧州，又以母辭。

translations.literal: Appointed prefect of Dengzhou, he again declined on account of his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When named prefect of Dengzhou, he again begged off to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 或指為避事，范仲淹言於朝曰：「張昪豈避事者？」

translations.literal: Some pointed to this as evasion of duty; Fan Zhongyan said at court: "Is Zhang Bian one to evade responsibility?"
translations.idiomatic: Some called this shirking duty, but Fan Zhongyan told the court: "Zhang Bian is no shirker."

sentences.zh: 乃許歸養。

translations.literal: Permission was granted for him to return home to care for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The court allowed him to go home and support his mother.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部判官、開封府推官，至知雜御史。

translations.literal: He served successively as Revenue Section judge, investigator of the Kaifeng prefecture, and eventually as Auxiliary Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He held in turn the posts of Revenue Section judge, Kaifeng investigator, and finally auxiliary censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 張堯佐緣恩驟用，知開封府；

translations.literal: Zhang Yaozhuo was suddenly promoted through favor and made prefect of Kaifeng;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yaozhuo, raised overnight through imperial favor, was made prefect of Kaifeng;

sentences.zh: 內侍楊懷敏夜直禁中，而衛士為變，皆極論之。

translations.literal: the eunuch Yang Huaimin stood night watch in the Forbidden Palace, and when the guards mutinied—all these Bian vigorously criticized in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: the eunuch Yang Huaimin kept night duty inside the palace, and when the guard corps rebelled—Bian condemned each of these abuses in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 昪性質樸，不善擇言，至斥張貴妃為一婦人，謂懷敏得志，將不減劉季述。

translations.literal: Bian's nature was plain and blunt; he was not skilled at choosing his words, going so far as to denounce Consort Zhang as "a woman," and saying that if Huaimin got his way he would be no less than Liu Jishu.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and blunt by nature, Bian chose his words poorly: he dismissed Consort Zhang as "just a woman" and warned that if Huaimin had his way he would rival the tyrant eunuch Liu Jishu.

sentences.zh: 仁宗讀之不懌，以語陳升之。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong read it with displeasure and spoke of it to Chen Shengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong read the memorial with annoyance and mentioned it to Chen Shengzhi.

sentences.zh: 升之曰：「此忠直之言，不激切，則聖意不可回矣。」

translations.literal: Chen Shengzhi said: "This is loyal and forthright speech; without such sharpness the sovereign's mind cannot be turned."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shengzhi replied: "These are loyal, straight words; unless they cut sharply, Your Majesty's mind will not be moved."

sentences.zh: 帝乃解。

translations.literal: The Emperor then relented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased.

sentences.zh: 以天章閣待制知慶州，改龍圖閣直學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: Bian was made Drafting Official at the Hall of Heavenly Writings and prefect of Qingzhou, then changed to Attendant Academician of the Hall of Dragon Illustrations and prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed drafting official at the Hall of Heavenly Writings and prefect of Qingzhou, then promoted to attendant academician of the Hall of Dragon Illustrations and prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，青唐蕃部藺氈，世居古渭，積與夏人有隙，懼而獻其地。

translations.literal: At first the Qingtang Tibetan chieftain Moqin had long lived at ancient Guwei, accumulated grievances with the Xia, and in fear surrendered his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Qingtang Tibetan leader Moqin, whose people had long dwelt at ancient Guwei, had built up enmity with the Xia and, in fear, offered up his lands.

sentences.zh: 攝帥范祥無遠慮，亟城之。

translations.literal: The acting commander Fan Xiang lacked far-sighted planning and hastily built a fort there.
translations.idiomatic: Acting commander Fan Xiang, lacking long-range judgment, hurriedly walled the place.

sentences.zh: 諸族畏其偪，舉兵叛。

translations.literal: The various tribes, fearing encroachment, rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The surrounding clans, alarmed by the pressure, took up arms in revolt.

sentences.zh: 昪至，請棄勿城。

translations.literal: When Bian arrived he requested that it be abandoned and not fortified.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post, Bian asked that the site be given up and left unwalled.

sentences.zh: 詔戶部副使傅求審視之，以為不可棄，與昪議殊。

translations.literal: The court ordered Deputy Finance Commissioner Fu Qiu to inspect the matter; he judged it could not be abandoned, and his opinion differed from Bian's.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent Deputy Finance Commissioner Fu Qiu to review the question; he ruled that the fort must be kept, contrary to Bian's view.

sentences.zh: 先是，副總管劉渙討叛羌，逗撓不時進，昪命他將郭恩代之，羌乃潰去。

translations.literal: Previously the vice commander-in-chief Liu Huan had been sent to suppress the rebellious Qiang but dallied and did not advance in time; Bian ordered another general, Guo En, to replace him, and the Qiang then broke and fled.
