translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Vice Commander Liu Huan had been dispatched against the rebel Qiang but stalled and failed to press the attack; Bian replaced him with General Guo En, and the Qiang forces scattered.

sentences.zh: 渙黜其功，讕訟恩多殺老稚，以撼昪。

translations.literal: Huan dismissed his achievements and slandered En for excessive killing of old and young, aiming to undermine Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Huan belittled the victory and accused En of slaughtering the aged and young, seeking to shake Bian's position.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命張方平守秦，徙渙涇原，亦徙昪青州。

translations.literal: The court ordered Zhang Fangping to hold Qinzhou, transferred Huan to Jingyuan, and also transferred Bian to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Zhang Fangping to hold Qinzhou, moved Huan to Jingyuan, and reassigned Bian to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 將罪昪，方平辭曰：「渙、昪有階級，今互言而兩罷帥，不可為也。」

translations.literal: About to punish Bian, Fangping declined, saying: "Huan and Bian have ranks; now they accuse each other and both commanders are dismissed—that cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: When the court was about to punish Bian, Fangping objected: "Huan and Bian stand in ranked posts; if mutual accusations now bring down both commanders, that precedent must not be set."

sentences.zh: 昪乃復留。

translations.literal: Bian was then allowed to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was therefore kept in office.

sentences.zh: 至和二年，召兼侍讀，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhihe he was summoned and concurrently made Lecturer-in-Attendance, and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhihe he was recalled, made lecturer-in-attendance as well, and appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 劉沆在相位，以御史范師道、趙抃嘗攻其惡，陰欲出之。

translations.literal: Liu Hang held the chancellorship and, because censors Fan Shidao and Zhao Bian had previously attacked his misdeeds, secretly wanted to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hang occupied the chancellorship and, since censors Fan Shidao and Zhao Bian had assailed his misconduct, secretly sought to drive them out.

sentences.zh: 昪曰：「天子耳目之官，奈何用宰相怒而斥？」

translations.literal: Bian said: "They are the Son of Heaven's ears and eyes—how can they be dismissed because of a chief minister's anger?"
translations.idiomatic: Bian protested: "These are the emperor's eyes and ears—how can they be banished to satisfy a chancellor's wrath?"

sentences.zh: 上章力爭之，沆竟罷去。

translations.literal: He submitted memorials vigorously contesting it, and Hang was ultimately dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized fiercely in their defense, and Hang was finally removed.

sentences.zh: 帝見昪指切時事無所避，謂曰：「卿孤立，乃能如是。」

translations.literal: The Emperor saw that Bian's criticisms of current affairs were uncompromising and said: "You stand alone, yet you can act thus."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Bian speak bluntly on public affairs without evasion, the emperor said: "You stand alone, yet you dare so much."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣仰託聖主，致位侍從，是為不孤。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant relies on the sagely sovereign and has risen to attend as a close companion—that is not standing alone.
translations.idiomatic: Bian answered: "I lean on a sage ruler and have been raised to serve at court—I am not alone.

sentences.zh: 今陛下之臣，持祿養望者多，而赤心謀國者少，竊以為如陛下乃孤立爾。」

translations.literal: Now among Your Majesty's ministers, many hold their salaries and cultivate prestige, while few devote their true hearts to planning for the state; I venture to think it is Your Majesty who stands alone."
translations.idiomatic: Among Your Majesty's ministers today, many cling to salary and reputation while few give their whole hearts to the realm; it is Your Majesty, I think, who stands alone."

sentences.zh: 帝為之感動。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved to his core.

sentences.zh: 契丹主宗真遣使齎其畫像來，求帝畫像，未報而死。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler Zongzhen sent envoys bearing his portrait seeking the Emperor's portrait in return; before a reply came, he died.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor Zongzhen sent envoys with his painted likeness, asking for the Song emperor's portrait in exchange; before an answer could be sent, he died.

sentences.zh: 子洪基立，以為請，詔昪報聘，諭使更致新主像。

translations.literal: His son Hongji succeeded and renewed the request; the court ordered Bian to go on a return mission and instructed the envoys to bring a portrait of the new ruler.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongji succeeded and pressed the same request; the court dispatched Bian on a return embassy and told the envoys to present the new emperor's likeness.

sentences.zh: 契丹欲先得之，昪曰：「昔文成以弟為兄屈，尚先致敬，況今為伯父哉！」

translations.literal: The Khitan wanted to receive it first; Bian said: "Formerly Princess Wencheng, though humiliated by treating her brother as elder, still paid respects first—how much more so now when he is uncle to our emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan side insisted on receiving the portrait first; Bian replied: "Even Princess Wencheng, though forced to treat a younger brother as elder, still offered courtesy first—how much more should an uncle do so now!"

sentences.zh: 遂無以奪，乃復以洪基像來。

translations.literal: They could not prevail; they brought Hongji's portrait again.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to override him, they sent Hongji's portrait once more.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐三年，擢樞密副使，遷參知政事、樞密使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiayou he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, then transferred to Vice Grand Councilor and Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiayou he rose to vice commissioner of military affairs, then became vice grand councilor and commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 昪愛惜官資，凡內降所與，多持不下。

translations.literal: Bian cherished official rank and stipends; whenever the inner court issued private decrees granting favors, he often withheld approval.
translations.idiomatic: Bian guarded official appointments jealously and often refused to ratify favors issued by private edict from the inner court.

sentences.zh: 見帝春秋高，前後屢進言儲嗣事，卒與韓琦同決策。

translations.literal: Seeing the Emperor's advanced age, he repeatedly urged matters of the heir apparent and ultimately decided together with Han Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Noting the emperor's great age, he repeatedly pressed the question of the succession and finally settled it together with Han Qi.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，請老，帝曰：「太尉勤勞王家，詎可遽去？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Bian requested retirement; the Emperor said: "Grand Marshal, you have served the royal house with diligence—how can you leave so soon?"
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Bian asked to retire; the emperor said: "Grand Marshal, you have toiled long for the throne—how can you depart so quickly?"

sentences.zh: 但命五日一至院，進見無蹈舞。

translations.literal: He was merely ordered to come to the bureau once every five days, and when granted audience he need not perform the bowing dance.
translations.idiomatic: He was told only to attend the bureau once every five days and, when received in audience, was excused from the bowing dance.

sentences.zh: 司馬光上疏言：「近歲以來，大臣年高者皆不敢自安其位，言事者欲以為名，又從而攻之。

translations.literal: Sima Guang submitted a memorial saying: "In recent years ministers of advanced age have all been unable to rest easy in their posts; those who speak out want to make a name and others attack them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang memorialized: "In recent years elder ministers have scarcely been able to hold their posts in peace; critics seek renown by attacking them, and others join the assault.

sentences.zh: 使其人無可取，雖少壯何為？

translations.literal: If such a person has nothing to commend him, what good is youth?
translations.idiomatic: If a man has nothing to offer, what use is his youth?

sentences.zh: 果有益於時，雖老何傷？

translations.literal: If he truly benefits the times, what harm in age?
translations.idiomatic: If he truly serves the age, what injury is there in age?

sentences.zh: 昪為人忠謹清直，不可干以私，若使且居其位，於事亦未有曠廢也。」

translations.literal: Bian is loyal, careful, pure, and upright; he cannot be swayed by private interests; if he remains in office for a time, affairs will not be neglected."
translations.idiomatic: Bian is loyal, prudent, upright, and incorruptible; let him keep his post awhile and the business of state will not suffer."

sentences.zh: 昪請不已，始賜告，令養疾，遂以彰信軍節度使、同中書門下平章事判許州，改鎮河陽三城。

translations.literal: Bian's requests continued without end; he was finally granted leave to recuperate, then made Military Commissioner of the Zhangxin Army and Grand Councilor of the same rank administering Xuzhou, then transferred to the Three Cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bian kept petitioning until he was at last granted sick leave, then made military commissioner of the Zhangxin Army and a grand councilor of equal rank administering Xuzhou, later transferred to the Three Cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 拜太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 熙寧十年薨，年八十六。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xining he died, at age eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Xining, aged eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒兼侍中，諡曰康節。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Minister of Works and concurrent Palace Attendant, with the posthumous name Kangjie.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Minister of Works and concurrent palace attendant, with the posthumous name Kangjie.

sentences.zh: 趙槩，字叔平，南京虞城人。

translations.literal: Zhao Gai, courtesy name Shuping, was a native of Yucheng in the Southern Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gai, styled Shuping, came from Yucheng in the Southern Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 少篤學自力，器識宏遠，為一時名輩稱許。

translations.literal: In youth he was devoted to study and self-reliant, with broad vision and capacity, praised by the leading men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied with fierce discipline and stood on his own strength; his breadth of mind won praise from the foremost men of the day.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，通判海州，為集賢校理、開封府推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served as vice prefect of Haizhou, then as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and investigator of the Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he was vice prefect of Haizhou, then collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and investigator for Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 奏事殿中，仁宗面賜銀緋。

translations.literal: When memorializing in the palace hall, Emperor Renzong personally bestowed silver and crimson robes upon him.
translations.idiomatic: While presenting business in the palace hall, he received from Emperor Renzong's own hand robes of silver and crimson.

sentences.zh: 出知洪州，州城西南薄章江，有泛溢之虞，槩作石堤二百丈，高五丈，以障其沖，水不為患。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Hongzhou—the city southwest adjoined the Zhang River and faced flood risk—Gai built a stone dike two hundred zhang long and five zhang high to block the surge, and the water no longer threatened.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned prefect of Hongzhou, he found the city vulnerable on the southwest where it pressed the Zhang River; he raised a stone embankment two hundred zhang long and five zhang high to break the flood, and the river no longer menaced the town.

sentences.zh: 僚吏鄭陶、饒奭挾持郡事，為不法，前守莫能制。

translations.literal: Staff members Zheng Tao and Rao Shi manipulated county affairs unlawfully; prior prefects could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates Zheng Tao and Rao Shi had seized control of county business and broken the law; earlier prefects had been unable to restrain them.

sentences.zh: 州之歸化卒，皆故時群盜。

translations.literal: The garrison troops of Guihua in the prefecture were all former bandit gangs.
translations.idiomatic: The Guihua garrison in the prefecture was made up entirely of former outlaw bands.

sentences.zh: 奭造飛語曰：「卒得廩米陳惡，有怨言，不更給善米，且生變。」

translations.literal: Shi fabricated rumors: "The troops received stale, bad grain from the granary and have grievances; if good grain is not issued anew, mutiny will follow."
translations.idiomatic: Shi spread a rumor: "The soldiers were given spoiled grain from the storehouse and are angry; unless fresh grain is issued, there will be trouble."

sentences.zh: 槩不答。

translations.literal: Gai did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Gai ignored it.

sentences.zh: 卒有自容州戍逃歸而犯夜者，斬之以徇，因收陶、奭抵罪，闔府股栗。

translations.literal: When a soldier who had deserted from garrison at Rongzhou was caught breaking curfew, Gai executed him as a warning, then had Tao and Shi prosecuted and convicted; the whole prefecture trembled.
translations.idiomatic: When a deserter from the Rongzhou garrison was caught violating curfew, Gai executed him publicly, then prosecuted Tao and Shi; the entire prefecture shook with fear.

sentences.zh: 加直集賢院、知青州。

translations.literal: He was added as Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐失舉澠池令張誥免，久乃起，監密州酒。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for failing to recommend the magistrate of Mianchi, Zhang Gao; after a long interval he was restored to supervise the wine monopoly at Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He lost office for not recommending the Mianchi magistrate Zhang Gao; only after a long interval was he restored to supervise the wine tax at Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 知滁州，山東有寇李二過境上，告人曰：「我東人也，公嘗為青州，民愛之如父母，我不忍犯。」

translations.literal: As prefect of Chuzhou, when the bandit Li Er of Shandong passed through the border he told people: "I am from the east; the Lord served Qingzhou and the people loved him like parents—I cannot bear to violate him."
translations.idiomatic: While prefect of Chuzhou, when the Shandong bandit Li Er crossed the border he told the locals: "I am an easterner too; when the Lord governed Qingzhou the people loved him as parents—I will not harm his district."

sentences.zh: 率眾去。

translations.literal: He led his band away.
translations.idiomatic: He marched his followers away.

sentences.zh: 召修起居注。

translations.literal: He was summoned to compile the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was called up to help compile the Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修後至，朝廷欲驟用之，難於越次。

translations.literal: When Ouyang Xiu arrived later, the court wished to promote him quickly but found it difficult to leapfrog seniority.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang Xiu came later, the court wanted to advance him swiftly but hesitated to skip over senior men.

sentences.zh: 槩聞，請郡，除天章閣待制、糾察在京刑獄，修遂知制誥。

translations.literal: Gai heard and requested a prefectural post; he was made Drafting Official at the Hall of Heavenly Writings and Inspector of Capital Punishments, and Xiu was given drafting duties for edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, Gai asked for a provincial appointment; he was made drafting official at the Hall of Heavenly Writings and inspector of capital punishments, while Xiu received the drafting post for edicts.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，槩始代之。

translations.literal: A year later, Gai finally replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: After a year Gai at last succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 郊祀，當任子、進階爵，乞回其恩，封母郡太君。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice, when he was entitled to ennoble his son and advance rank, he begged to redirect that favor and ennoble his mother as Lady of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifice, though entitled to ennoble his son and raise his own rank, he asked instead to transfer the honor and ennoble his mother as Lady of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 宰相謂曰：「君即為學士，擬封不久矣。」

translations.literal: The chief minister said: "You will soon be made Academician; ennoblement will follow shortly."
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister told him: "You will soon become an academician; such honors can wait a little."

sentences.zh: 槩曰：「母年八十二，願及今拜君賜以為榮。」

translations.literal: Gai said: "My mother is eighty-two; I wish to receive Your Majesty's gift now as an honor."
translations.idiomatic: Gai replied: "My mother is eighty-two; I want her to receive the emperor's grace while she still can."

sentences.zh: 乃許之，後遂為例。

translations.literal: Permission was granted, and it later became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved, and afterward became established practice.

sentences.zh: 蘇舜欽等以群飲逐，槩言：「預會者皆館閣名士，舉而棄之，觖士大夫望，非國之福也。」

translations.literal: When Su Shunqin and others were expelled for group drinking, Gai said: "Those who attended were all distinguished men of the academies and pavilions; to select and discard them disappoints the hopes of scholar-officials—not a blessing to the state."
translations.idiomatic: After Su Shunqin and others were banished for communal drinking, Gai argued: "Those present were eminent men of the halls and pavilions; to cast them out wounds the hopes of the scholar-official class and does the realm no good."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply came.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 求知蘇州，終母喪，入為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He requested to know Suzhou; after completing mourning for his mother he entered as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to serve at Suzhou; when his mourning was finished he returned as a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 聘契丹，契丹主會獵，請賦《信誓如山河詩》」，詩成，親酌玉杯為槩勸，且授侍臣劉六符素扇，寫之納袖中，其禮重如此。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to the Khitan; at a hunt the Khitan ruler asked him to compose the poem "Oaths as Firm as Mountains and Rivers"; when the poem was finished, the ruler personally poured wine from a jade cup to urge Gai, and gave his attendant Liu Liufu a plain fan on which to write it and put it in his sleeve—the courtesy was so great.
translations.idiomatic: On embassy to the Khitan, at a royal hunt the Khitan emperor asked him to compose the poem "Oaths as Firm as Mountains and Rivers"; when the verses were done, the emperor himself filled a jade cup to toast Gai and had his attendant Liu Liufu copy the poem on a plain fan and tuck it into his sleeve—such was the honor shown him.

sentences.zh: 還，兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: On his return he was additionally made Lecturer-in-Attendance Academician.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he was also made lecturer-in-attendance academician.

sentences.zh: 諫官郭申錫論事忤旨，帝欲加罪，槩曰：「陛下始面諭申錫毋面從，今黜之，何以示天下？」

translations.literal: When remonstrating official Guo Shenxi spoke against the imperial will and the Emperor wished to punish him, Gai said: "Your Majesty first instructed Shenxi face to face not to agree outwardly; now if you dismiss him, how will that be shown to the world?"
translations.idiomatic: When remonstrance official Guo Shenxi offended the throne and the emperor meant to punish him, Gai said: "Your Majesty personally told Shenxi not to flatter you to your face; if you now remove him, what lesson will the empire draw?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 槩秉心和平，與人無怨怒。

translations.literal: Gai kept his heart peaceful and bore no resentment toward others.
translations.idiomatic: Gai held a tranquil heart and nursed no grudges against others.

sentences.zh: 雖在事如不言，然陰以利物者為不少，議者以比劉寬、婁師德。

translations.literal: Although in office he was as if he did not speak, yet those he secretly benefited were not few; commentators compared him to Liu Kuan and Lou Shide.
translations.idiomatic: Though in office he seemed to say little, he quietly did much to help others; observers likened him to Liu Kuan and Lou Shide.

sentences.zh: 坐張誥貶六年，念之終不衰，誥死，恤其家備至。

translations.literal: Because of Zhang Gao he was demoted for six years; his regard for him never waned. When Gao died, he cared for his family with utmost thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: He had been demoted for six years on account of Zhang Gao, yet his affection never faded; when Gao died, he saw to his household with every care.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修遇槩素薄，又躐知制誥，及修有獄，槩獨抗章明其罪，言為仇者所中傷，不可以天下法為人報怨。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu had always held Gai in low regard, and had moreover leapfrogged ahead to draft edicts. When Xiu fell into legal trouble, Gai alone submitted a memorial stating his offense plainly, saying he had been wounded by enemies and that one must not use the laws of the realm to settle personal scores.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu had long looked down on Gai and had vaulted past him to the post of drafter of edicts. When Xiu was caught in a legal case, Gai alone submitted a forthright memorial on his guilt, arguing that he had been struck down by foes and that the laws of the empire must not serve private vengeance.

sentences.zh: 修得解，始服其長者。

translations.literal: When Xiu was cleared, he at last recognized Gai's magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiu was exonerated, he came at last to respect Gai as a man of stature.

sentences.zh: 為鄆州時，吏按前守馮浩侵公使錢三十萬，當以職田租償。

translations.literal: When he was prefect of Yun, officials investigated the former prefect Feng Hao for embezzling three hundred thousand in envoy funds; he was liable to repay it from the rent of his official fields.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as prefect of Yun, clerks found that the former prefect Feng Hao had misappropriated three hundred thousand in public envoy funds and was obliged to make restitution from the rent of his official fields.

sentences.zh: 槩知其貧，為代以己奉。

translations.literal: Gai knew he was poor and paid it on his behalf out of his own salary.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Feng's poverty, Gai paid the sum for him out of his own stipend.

sentences.zh: 其平生所為類此。

translations.literal: His conduct throughout his life was mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Most of what he did in his life was of this kind.

sentences.zh: 槩初名禋，嘗夢神人金書名簿有「趙槩」，遂更云。

translations.literal: Gai had originally been named Yin. Once he dreamed of a divine being with a golden-written register bearing the name 'Zhao Gai,' and so changed his name accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Gai had first been named Yin. He once dreamed of a god holding a golden register on which stood the name Zhao Gai, and thereafter changed his name.

sentences.zh: 胡宿，字武平，常州晉陵人。

translations.literal: Hu Su, courtesy name Wuping, was a native of Jinling in Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Su, styled Wuping, was a native of Jinling in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登第，為揚子尉。

translations.literal: After passing the examinations, he was appointed sheriff of Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the examinations, he was made sheriff of Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 縣大水，民被溺，令不能救，宿率公私船活數千人。

translations.literal: When the county suffered great flooding and the people were drowning, the magistrate could not save them. Su led public and private boats and saved several thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: When the county was struck by great floods and people were drowning, the magistrate could not rescue them; Su mustered official and private boats and saved several thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 以薦為館閣校勘，進集賢校理。

translations.literal: Through recommendation he became a collator in the Hall of Literature and advanced to proofreader in the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was made a collator in the Hall of Literature, then promoted to proofreader in the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 通判宣州，囚有殺人者，將抵死，宿疑而訊之，囚憚箠楚不敢言。

translations.literal: As vice prefect of Xuan Prefecture, there was a prisoner convicted of murder who was about to be executed. Su had doubts and questioned him, but the prisoner feared the beating and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as vice prefect of Xuan, a man condemned for murder was about to die. Su questioned him with misgivings, but the prisoner, fearing the rod, would not speak.

sentences.zh: 辟左右復問，久乃云：「旦將之田，縣吏縛以赴官，莫知其故。」

translations.literal: He dismissed those around him and questioned him again. After a long time the man finally said: 'At dawn I was going to my fields when county clerks bound me and escorted me to the office—I do not know why.'
translations.idiomatic: Su sent his attendants away and questioned him again. At length the man said, "At dawn I was on my way to the fields when county clerks bound me and brought me to court. I do not know why."

sentences.zh: 宿取具獄繙閱，探其本辭，蓋婦人與所私者殺其夫，而執平民以告也。

translations.literal: Su took the completed case record and read through it, probing the original accusation: it turned out a woman and her lover had killed her husband and had seized an ordinary man to accuse instead.
translations.idiomatic: Su took up the completed dossier and traced the original charge: a woman and her paramour had murdered her husband and had seized an innocent man to stand accused in his place.

sentences.zh: 知湖州，前守滕宗諒大興學校，費錢數十萬。

translations.literal: As prefect of Hu, the former prefect Teng Zongliang had greatly expanded the county schools, spending several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Su governed Hu Prefecture, the former prefect Teng Zongliang had greatly enlarged the schools there, spending several hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 宗諒去，通判、僚吏皆疑以為欺，不肯書歷。

translations.literal: When Zongliang departed, the vice prefect and staff all suspected fraud and refused to sign the accounts.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongliang left, the vice prefect and his colleagues all suspected fraud and refused to sign off on the accounts.

sentences.zh: 宿誚之曰：「君輩佐滕侯久矣，苟有過，盍不早正？

translations.literal: Su reproached them, saying: 'You all have long served Master Teng—if there were fault, why not correct it early?
translations.idiomatic: Su rebuked them, saying, "You have long served under Master Teng. If there was wrongdoing, why did you not set it right at once?

sentences.zh: 乃陰拱以觀，俟其去而非之，豈昔人分謗之意乎？」

translations.literal: Yet you secretly held your hands and watched, waiting till he had left to denounce him—is that the meaning of sharing blame as men of old did?'
translations.idiomatic: Instead you folded your hands in silence, waited until he had gone, and then condemned him—is that what the ancients meant by sharing blame?"

sentences.zh: 坐者大慚謝。

translations.literal: Those present were deeply ashamed and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Those seated there were deeply ashamed and apologized.

sentences.zh: 其後湖學為東南最，宿之力為多。

translations.literal: Afterwards the Hu Prefecture schools became the finest in the southeast, largely through Su's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the schools of Hu became the best in the southeast, largely through Su's exertions.

sentences.zh: 築石塘百里，捍水患，民號曰胡公塘，而學者為立生祠。

translations.literal: He built a stone embankment a hundred li long to ward off flooding. The people called it Lord Hu's Embankment, and scholars erected a living shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: He built a stone dike a hundred li long to hold back floodwaters. The people named it Lord Hu's Dike, and scholars raised a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 久之，為兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: After some time he became transport commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made transport commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 召修起居注、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was summoned to compile the Daily Record and to draft edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to compile the Daily Record and to serve as drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 入內都知楊懷敏坐衛士之變，斥為和州都監，未幾，召入復故職。

translations.literal: Palace intendant Yang Huaimin, implicated in the guards' mutiny, was demoted to military supervisor of He Prefecture. Before long he was recalled and restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Intendant Yang Huaimin, implicated in the guards' uprising, was demoted to military supervisor of He Prefecture; before long he was recalled and restored to his old office.

sentences.zh: 宿封還詞頭，且言：「懷敏得不窮治誅死，已幸，豈宜覆在左右？」

translations.literal: Su returned the draft edict sealed and said: 'That Huaimin was not prosecuted to the full extent and put to death was already good fortune—how can he properly be placed again at the emperor's side?'
translations.idiomatic: Su sealed and returned the draft edict, saying, "That Huaimin was not fully prosecuted and put to death was already mercy enough. How can he rightly be placed again at the emperor's side?"

sentences.zh: 命遂寢。

translations.literal: The order was thereupon shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was thereupon dropped.

sentences.zh: 慶曆六年，京東、兩河地震，登、萊尤甚。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qingli, Jingdong and the Two He regions suffered earthquakes; Deng and Lai were hit especially hard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qingli, earthquakes struck Jingdong and the Two He circuits; Deng and Lai suffered most severely.

sentences.zh: 宿兼通陰陽五行災異之學，乃上疏曰：「明年丁亥，歲之刑德，皆在北宮。

translations.literal: Su was versed also in yin-yang, the Five Phases, and theories of portents, and submitted a memorial saying: 'Next year is dinghai; the year's punitive and beneficent influences both lie in the Northern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Su was also versed in yin-yang, the Five Phases, and the lore of omens, and submitted a memorial saying, "Next year is dinghai; the year's chastising and beneficent forces both lie in the Northern Palace.

sentences.zh: 陰生於午，而極於亥。

translations.literal: Yin is born at wu and reaches its extreme at hai.
translations.idiomatic: Yin is born at wu and reaches its height at hai.

sentences.zh: 然陰猶強而未即伏，陽猶微而不能勝，此所以震也。

translations.literal: Yet yin is still strong and has not yet submitted, while yang is still weak and cannot overcome it—this is why the earth quakes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet yin remains strong and has not yet yielded, while yang is still faint and cannot prevail—that is why the earth trembles.

sentences.zh: 是謂龍戰之會，其位在乾。

translations.literal: This is called the meeting of the contending dragons; its position is in Qian.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is called the meeting where dragons contend; its station lies in Qian.

sentences.zh: 若西北二邊不動，恐有內盜起於河朔。

translations.literal: If the two northwestern frontiers do not stir, I fear internal bandits may rise in Heshuo.
translations.idiomatic: If the two northwestern frontiers do not move, I fear internal rebels may rise in Heshuo.

sentences.zh: 又登、萊視京師，為東北少陽之位，今二州置金坑，多聚民鑿山谷，陽氣耗泄，故陰乘而動。

translations.literal: Moreover, Deng and Lai face the capital as the northeast position of lesser yang. Now in both prefectures gold mines have been established and masses of people gathered to dig in the mountains—yang energy is drained away, and so yin seizes the occasion to stir.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Deng and Lai lie toward the capital in the northeast seat of lesser yang. Now in both prefectures gold pits have been opened and crowds gathered to quarry the hills; yang is spent and dissipated, and yin takes advantage to stir.

sentences.zh: 宜即禁止，以寧地道。」

translations.literal: They should be forbidden at once to settle the earth's way.'
translations.idiomatic: These works should be forbidden at once to quiet the way of earth."

sentences.zh: 時以為迂闊。

translations.literal: At the time this was thought impractical and far-fetched.
translations.idiomatic: At the time people judged this impractical and far-fetched.

sentences.zh: 明年，王則果以貝州叛。

translations.literal: The next year Wang Ze did indeed rebel at Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wang Ze did indeed rebel at Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 皇祐五年正月，會靈宮災，是歲冬至，郊，以二帝並配。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year of Huangyou, the Huiling Palace burned. That year at the winter solstice the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice, with both emperors enshrined together.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year of Huangyou the Huiling Palace burned. That winter solstice the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice with both emperors jointly enshrined.

sentences.zh: 明年大旱，宿言：「五行，火，禮也。

translations.literal: The next year there was great drought. Su said: 'Among the Five Phases, fire corresponds to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The next year there was severe drought. Su said, "Among the Five Phases, fire belongs to ritual.

sentences.zh: 去歲火而今又旱，其應在禮，此殆郊丘並配之失也。」

translations.literal: Last year there was fire, and now drought—the omen lies in ritual; this is likely the fault of enshrining both at the suburban altar together.'
translations.idiomatic: Last year there was fire, and now drought—the response lies in ritual. This is likely the error of joint enshrinement at the suburban altar."

sentences.zh: 即建言並配非古，宜用迭配如初。

translations.literal: He promptly advocated that joint enshrinement was not ancient practice and that alternating enshrinement as before should be used.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon argued that joint enshrinement was not the ancient way and that alternating enshrinement should be restored as before.

sentences.zh: 時議者謂士大夫言，七十當致仕，其不知止者，請令有司按籍舉行之。

translations.literal: At the time commentators said that scholars and officials, when they reached seventy, ought to retire; those who did not know when to stop—they requested that the relevant offices examine the registers and enforce this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some argued that officials who reached seventy ought to retire, and that those who did not know when to stop should be identified from the registers and compelled to do so.

sentences.zh: 宿以為非優老之義，當少緩其期法：武吏察其任事與否，勿斷以年；

translations.literal: Su held that this was not the meaning of honoring the aged, and that the deadline should be relaxed somewhat: for military officers, examine whether they can still perform their duties—do not decide by age alone;
translations.idiomatic: Su held that this was not true honor for the aged and that the rule should be eased somewhat: for military officers, judge whether they can still perform their duties rather than fixing the matter by age alone;

sentences.zh: 文吏使得自陳而全其節。

translations.literal: for civil officers, allow them to petition for themselves and preserve their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: for civil officers, let them petition on their own behalf and preserve their dignity.

sentences.zh: 及言皇祐新樂與舊樂難並用；

translations.literal: He also said that the new music of Huangyou and the old music were hard to use together;
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the new music of Huangyou could not readily be used together with the old;

sentences.zh: 禮部間歲一貢士不便，當用三年之制。

translations.literal: that the Ministry of Rites' practice of presenting scholars every other year was inconvenient, and the three-year system should be used.
translations.idiomatic: and that the Ministry of Rites' biennial presentation of candidates was inconvenient and that the three-year system should be restored.

sentences.zh: 皆如其言。

translations.literal: In each case his counsel was followed.
translations.idiomatic: In each case the court adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 唐介貶嶺南，帝遣中使護以往。

translations.literal: Tang Jie was demoted to Lingnan; the emperor sent a palace envoy to escort him thither.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jie was demoted to Lingnan, and the emperor dispatched a palace envoy to escort him on his way.

sentences.zh: 宿言：「事有不可測，介如不幸道死，陛下受殺直臣之名。」

translations.literal: Su said: 'Matters cannot all be foreseen—if Jie should unhappily die on the road, Your Majesty would bear the name of having killed a straight official.'
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Things cannot all be foreseen. If Jie should die by misfortune on the road, Your Majesty would bear the name of having killed a loyal remonstrator."

sentences.zh: 帝悟，追還使者。

translations.literal: The emperor took his point and recalled the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his meaning and recalled the envoy.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士，知審官、刑院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin academician and put in charge of the Bureau for Review of Appointments and the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician and placed in charge of the Bureau for Review of Appointments and the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 李仲昌開六塔河，民被害，詔獄薄其罪。

translations.literal: Li Zhongchang had opened the Six Pagodas Canal and the people suffered harm; an imperial inquiry was ordered with lenient punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchang had opened the Six Pagodas Canal to the people's harm, and an imperial inquiry was ordered with lenient punishment.

sentences.zh: 宿請斬以謝河北，仲昌由是南竄。

translations.literal: Su requested execution to appease Hebei; Zhongchang was thereby driven into exile in the south.
translations.idiomatic: Su requested that he be executed to appease Hebei, and Zhongchang was thereby driven into exile in the south.

sentences.zh: 袞國公主下降，將行冊禮。

translations.literal: Princess Guoguo was to marry down, and the investiture ceremony was about to be performed.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Guoguo was to marry beneath her rank, and the investiture rites were about to be performed.

sentences.zh: 宿諫曰：「陛下昔封兩長主，未嘗冊命，今施之愛女，殆非漢明帝所謂『我子豈得與先帝子等』之義也。」

translations.literal: Su remonstrated: 'Your Majesty once enfeoffed your two elder princesses without ever performing investiture; to apply it now to a beloved daughter is hardly in the spirit of what Emperor Ming of Han said: "How can my children rank with the late emperor's children?"'
translations.idiomatic: Su remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty once enfeoffed your two elder princesses without ever granting investiture. To bestow it now upon a beloved daughter is hardly in the spirit of what Emperor Ming of Han meant when he said, 'How can my children rank with the late emperor's children?'"

sentences.zh: 涇州卒以折支不時給，出惡言，且欲相扇為亂。

translations.literal: Soldiers at Jing Prefecture, because their clothing allowance was not issued on time, uttered bitter words and even sought to stir one another to mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers at Jing Prefecture, because their cloth allowance was not issued on schedule, spoke bitterly and even sought to stir one another to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 既置於法，乃命劾三司吏。

translations.literal: After they had been punished by law, he ordered an investigation of the Three Departments clerks.
translations.idiomatic: After they had been punished according to law, he ordered an investigation of the clerks of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 三司使包拯護弗遣。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Three Departments Bao Zheng shielded them and would not send them forth.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of the Three Departments Bao Zheng shielded them and refused to send them forward.

sentences.zh: 宿曰：「涇卒固悖慢，然當給之物，越八十五日而不與，計吏安得為無罪？

translations.literal: Su said: 'The Jing soldiers were indeed insolent, yet the goods due them were withheld beyond eighty-five days—how can the accounting clerks be held blameless?
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "The Jing soldiers were indeed insolent, yet what was owed them was withheld for more than eighty-five days. How can the accounting clerks be held guiltless?

sentences.zh: 拯不知自省，公拒制命，紀綱益廢矣。」

translations.literal: Zheng does not know to examine himself, yet openly resists an imperial order—the fabric of discipline grows ever more ruined.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng does not know to examine himself, yet openly resists an imperial command—the bonds of discipline are being further undone."

sentences.zh: 拯懼，立遣吏。

translations.literal: In fear, Zheng immediately sent forth the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the consequences, Zheng at once sent the clerks forward.

sentences.zh: 韓琦守并州，請復其節鎮。

translations.literal: Han Qi, holding Bing Prefecture, requested restoration of its military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi, while governing Bing Prefecture, requested that its military commission be restored.

sentences.zh: 宿言：「參、商為仇讎之星。

translations.literal: Su said: 'Shen and Shang are stars of mutual enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Shen and Shang are stars of mutual enmity.

sentences.zh: 國家受命於商丘，而參為晉地。

translations.literal: The state received the Mandate at Shangqiu, while Shen corresponds to the land of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty received the Mandate at Shangqiu, while Shen corresponds to the land of Jin.

sentences.zh: 今欲崇晉，非國之利也。

translations.literal: To exalt Jin now would not benefit the state.
translations.idiomatic: To exalt Jin now would not serve the state's interest.

sentences.zh: 宋興削平四方，並最後服，故太宗不使列於方鎮，八十年矣，宜如故便。」

translations.literal: Since the founding of Song, when the four quarters were pacified, Bing submitted last; therefore Taizong did not list it among the frontier commands—it has been eighty years; it is best to leave matters as they were.'
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of Song, when the realm was pacified on all sides, Bing was the last to submit; therefore Taizong did not rank it among the frontier commands. Eighty years have passed—it is best to leave things as they are."

sentences.zh: 議遂止。

translations.literal: The proposal was thereupon halted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was thereupon dropped.

sentences.zh: 後琦秉政，卒復之。

translations.literal: Later, when Qi held power, it was in the end restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Qi came to power, the commission was restored after all.

sentences.zh: 宿為人清謹忠實，內剛外和，群居不嘩笑，與人言，必思而後對。

translations.literal: Su as a man was pure, careful, loyal, and truthful—firm within and gentle without. In company he never laughed aloud, and when he spoke with others he always thought first before answering.
translations.idiomatic: Su was pure, careful, loyal, and sincere—hard within and gentle without. In company he never laughed loudly, and when he spoke with others he always considered first and then replied.

sentences.zh: 故臨事重慎，不輒發，發亦不可回止。

translations.literal: Thus in affairs he was deeply cautious: he did not act rashly, and once he acted it could not be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in affairs he was grave and cautious: he did not act lightly, and once he acted there was no turning back.

sentences.zh: 居母喪三年，不至私室。

translations.literal: During three years of mourning for his mother he never entered his private quarters.
translations.idiomatic: During the three years of mourning for his mother he never entered his private chambers.

sentences.zh: 其當重任，尤顧惜大體。

translations.literal: When he held weighty office he was especially mindful of the larger good.
translations.idiomatic: When he bore heavy responsibility he was especially careful of the larger interest.

sentences.zh: 在審官、刑院，擇詳議官，有在選中者，嘗監征榷，以水災負課。

translations.literal: At the Bureau for Review of Appointments and the Bureau of Punishments, when selecting detailed-review officers, there was one on the appointment list who had once supervised tariff collection and, owing to flood, fell short on tax receipts.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Bureau for Review of Appointments and the Bureau of Punishments, he was selecting detailed-review officers when he found among the candidates one who had once supervised tax collection and, because of flood, had fallen short on receipts.

sentences.zh: 同列謂小累不足白，宿竟白之，而薦其才足用，仁宗聽納。

translations.literal: Colleagues said the minor flaw need not be reported, yet Su reported it all the same—and also recommended that his talent sufficed for use; Renzong accepted both.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues said the small blemish need not be reported to the throne, but Su reported it anyway and also recommended that the man's talent made him fit for service; Renzong accepted both.

sentences.zh: 同列退而誚曰：「公固欲白上，倘緣是不用，奈何？」

translations.literal: Colleagues withdrew and mocked him: 'You plainly meant to inform the throne—yet if he is not employed on that account, what then?'
translations.idiomatic: Afterward his colleagues withdrew and mocked him, saying, "You plainly meant to inform the throne—but if he is not appointed because of this, what then?"

sentences.zh: 宿曰：「彼之得否，不過一詳議官。

translations.literal: Su said: 'Whether he is employed or not affects no more than one detailed-review officer.
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Whether he is appointed or not concerns no more than one detailed-review officer.

sentences.zh: 宿平生以誠事主，今白首矣，忍以毫髮欺乎？

translations.literal: I have served my lord with sincerity all my life; now my hair is white—could I bear to deceive him over the slightest matter?
translations.idiomatic: I have served my lord with sincerity all my life. Now my hair is white—how could I deceive him over the slightest thing?

sentences.zh: 為之開陳，聽吾君自擇爾。」

translations.literal: I lay the facts before him and let my sovereign choose for himself—that is all.'
translations.idiomatic: I lay the facts before him and let my sovereign decide for himself—that is all."

sentences.zh: 少與一僧善，僧有秘術，能化瓦石為黃金。

translations.literal: In youth he was close to a monk who possessed a secret art and could transform tile and stone into gold.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was close to a monk who possessed a secret art and could turn tile and stone into gold.

sentences.zh: 且死，將以授宿，使葬之。

translations.literal: When the monk was about to die, he was going to pass it to Su and have him bury it with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the monk was near death, he meant to pass the art to Su and have him bury it with him.

sentences.zh: 宿曰：「後事當儘力，他非吾所冀也。」

translations.literal: Su said: 'I shall do my utmost for the funeral rites—that is all I desire.'
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "I shall do all I can for the funeral rites. That alone is what I desire."

sentences.zh: 僧嘆曰：「子之志，未可量也。」

translations.literal: The monk sighed and said: 'Your ambition cannot be measured.'
translations.idiomatic: The monk sighed and said, "Your resolve cannot be measured."

sentences.zh: 其篤行自勵，至於貴達，常如布衣時。

translations.literal: His steadfast conduct and self-discipline persisted even when he reached eminence—he remained as in the days when he wore plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: His earnest conduct and self-restraint endured even after he rose to high rank; he remained as he had been when he wore plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 子：宗炎；

translations.literal: His son: Zongyan;
translations.idiomatic: His son: Zongyan;

sentences.zh: 從子：宗愈、宗回。

translations.literal: His nephews: Zongyu and Zonghui.
translations.idiomatic: His nephews: Zongyu and Zonghui.

sentences.zh: 子 宗炎

translations.literal: Son: Zongyan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zongyan

sentences.zh: 宗炎，字彥聖，由將作監主簿鎖廳登第。

translations.literal: Zongyan, courtesy name Yansheng, passed the examinations through the locked-hall procedure as chief clerk in the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan, styled Yansheng, passed the examinations through the locked-hall procedure while serving as chief clerk in the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 為國子大宗正丞、開封府推官、考功吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He served as deputy director of the Grand Preceptorate of the National University, investigating censor of Kaifeng Prefecture, and director of merit evaluation in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy director of the National University's Grand Preceptorate, investigating censor of Kaifeng Prefecture, and director of merit evaluation in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 舊制，選人改京官，舉將小絓吏議，輒尼不行。

translations.literal: Under the old system, when a selected appointee was to be promoted to capital official, if the recommending superior had minor entanglements under clerical review, the promotion was always blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, when a selected appointee was to be promoted to capital official, if the recommending superior had minor blemishes under clerical review, the promotion was always blocked.

sentences.zh: 宗炎請先引見，俟舉者罪即追止，從之。

translations.literal: Zongyan requested that the appointee be presented first, and that if the recommender were found guilty the appointment be revoked—this was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan requested that the candidate first be presented to the throne and that if the recommender were found guilty the appointment be revoked at once; this was adopted.

sentences.zh: 哲宗崩，遼使來吊祭，宗炎以鴻臚少卿迓境上。

translations.literal: When Zhezong died, a Liao envoy came to offer condolence sacrifices; Zongyan, as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, welcomed him at the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong died, a Liao envoy came to offer condolence sacrifices, and Zongyan, as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, received him at the border.

sentences.zh: 使者不易服，宗炎以禮折之，須其聽命，乃相見。

translations.literal: The envoy would not change his dress; Zongyan used ceremony to rebuff him and would not meet until he obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy would not change his dress. Zongyan used ritual to rebuff him and would not meet until he submitted to the prescribed form.

sentences.zh: 暨還，升為卿。

translations.literal: Upon his return he was promoted to full director.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to full director.

sentences.zh: 初，父宿使遼，遼人重之。

translations.literal: Earlier, his father Su had served as envoy to Liao and the Liao people held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his father Su had served as envoy to Liao, and the Liao held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 其後宗炎婿鄧忠臣迓客，客問：「中外嘗有充使者否？」

translations.literal: Later Zongyan's son-in-law Deng Zhongchen welcomed an envoy; the envoy asked: 'Have there ever been envoys from within and without the court?'
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zongyan's son-in-law Deng Zhongchen received an envoy, the envoy asked, "Have there ever been envoys drawn from both within and without the court?"

sentences.zh: 忠臣以宿告，且言：「前使鴻臚，其子也。」

translations.literal: Zhongchen told him of Su, adding: 'The former envoy served as director of imperial sacrifices—and that was his son.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen told him of Su, adding, "The former envoy served as director of imperial sacrifices—and that man was his son."

sentences.zh: 客歎：「胡氏世不乏人。」

translations.literal: The envoy exclaimed: 'The Hu house has never lacked for men.'
translations.idiomatic: The envoy exclaimed, "The Hu house has never lacked worthy men."

sentences.zh: 俄以直龍圖閣知潁昌府，歷密州而卒。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed with the honorary title of drafting officer at the Dragon Diagram Hall and made prefect of Yingchang; he served also at Mi Prefecture and then died.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed with the honorary title Drafting Officer at the Dragon Diagram Hall and made prefect of Yingchang; he later governed Mi Prefecture and then died.

sentences.zh: 宗炎善為詩，藻思清婉。

translations.literal: Zongyan was skilled at poetry; his diction was clear and graceful.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan was skilled at poetry; his phrasing was clear and graceful.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修守亳，與客游郡圃，或誦其詩，修賞味不已，以為有鮑、謝風致。

translations.literal: When Ouyang Xiu was prefect of Bo, he wandered the prefectural garden with guests; someone recited Zongyan's poems, and Xiu, savoring them without end, judged them to possess the spirit of Bao Zhao and Xie Lingyun.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang Xiu governed Bo, he walked the prefectural garden with guests. Someone recited Zongyan's poems, and Xiu savored them endlessly, judging them to possess the spirit of Bao Zhao and Xie Lingyun.

sentences.zh: 其重之如此。

translations.literal: He valued him to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he held him.

sentences.zh: 從子 宗愈

translations.literal: Nephew Zongyu
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Zongyu

sentences.zh: 宗愈，字完夫，舉進士甲科，為光祿丞。

translations.literal: Zongyu, styled Wanfu, passed the jinshi examination in the first rank and served as vice director of the Imperial Household Service.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyu, courtesy name Wanfu, graduated jinshi with top honors and was appointed vice director of the Imperial Household Service.

sentences.zh: 宿得請杭州，英宗問：「子弟誰可繼者？」

translations.literal: When Su obtained leave to go to Hangzhou, Emperor Yingzong asked, "Which of your sons and younger brothers could succeed you?"
translations.idiomatic: When Su secured an appointment to Hangzhou, Emperor Yingzong asked which of his sons or nephews might follow in his footsteps.

sentences.zh: 以宗愈對。

translations.literal: He answered with Zongyu.
translations.idiomatic: He named Zongyu.

sentences.zh: 召試學士院。

translations.literal: Zongyu was summoned for a trial at the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyu was called to an examination at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，以為集賢校理。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Zongyu was made collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenzong's accession, he was appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 久之，兼史館檢討，遂同知諫院。

translations.literal: After some time he also served as reviser in the Historiography Institute, and then concurrently as vice director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In time he added the post of historiography reviser and then served concurrently as vice director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 殿內卒盜皇城器物，宗愈言：「唐長孫無忌不解佩刀入東上閣門，校尉論當死。

translations.literal: Palace attendants stole items from the Imperial City; Zongyu said, "When Tang's Zhangsun Wuji unknowingly entered the Eastern Upper Gate bearing a sword, the gate guards were judged worthy of death.
translations.idiomatic: When inner-palace attendants stole property from the Imperial City, Zongyu argued: "In Tang times Zhangsun Wuji once entered the Eastern Upper Gate still wearing his sword through ignorance, and the gate guards were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 今禁卒為盜，而入內都知不能覺察，願正其罪。」

translations.literal: Now forbidden troops commit theft, yet the director of the inner palace failed to detect it; I ask that their crimes be properly punished."
translations.idiomatic: Today forbidden troops turn thief, and the director of the inner palace never noticed—let their offenses be judged as they deserve."

sentences.zh: 殿帥直廬在長慶門內，久而自置隸圉。

translations.literal: The commandant of the palace guard's duty quarters was inside the Changqing Gate; after a long while he privately set up stable hands of his own.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guard commandant's duty station lay within Changqing Gate; over time he had begun to employ private grooms.

sentences.zh: 宗愈曰：「嚴禁旅，所以杜奸宄也。

translations.literal: Zongyu said, "Strict guard discipline exists to shut out treachery and wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyu said, "The guard exists to keep out plotters and malcontents.

sentences.zh: 奈何令私人得為之？

translations.literal: How can private persons be allowed to do this?
translations.idiomatic: Why should private retainers be permitted inside?

sentences.zh: 萬一凶黠者竄名其間，將不可悔。

translations.literal: If some vicious and cunning man should slip in among them, it will be beyond regret.
translations.idiomatic: Should some ruthless schemer hide among them, the harm would be irreparable.

sentences.zh: 請易募老卒。」

translations.literal: I ask that veteran soldiers be recruited instead."
translations.idiomatic: Recruit seasoned soldiers openly instead."

sentences.zh: 王安石用李定為御史，宗愈言：「御史當用學士及丞、雜論薦，又須官博士、員外郎。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi appointed Li Ding censor, Zongyu said, "A censor should be chosen from academicians and from vice directors and miscellaneous recommendees, and must hold the rank of erudite or outer-office gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi made Li Ding a censor, Zongyu protested: "Censors ought to come from the Hanlin and from recommended vice directors and staff officers, and must already hold erudite or outer-office rank.

sentences.zh: 今定以幕職不因薦得之，是殆一齣執政意，即大臣不法，誰復言之？」

translations.literal: Now Ding obtained the post as a staff officer without recommendation—this is nearly carrying out the chief minister's whim; if even grand ministers break the law, who will speak up again?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Ding gained the post as a staff aide without any recommendation—barely veiled favoritism from the chief minister. Once great ministers flout the law, who will dare object?"

sentences.zh: 蘇頌、李大臨不草制，坐絀；

translations.literal: Su Song and Li Daxin refused to draft the appointment edict and were demoted in rank;
translations.idiomatic: Su Song and Li Daxin declined to draft the appointment and were reduced in rank;

sentences.zh: 宗愈又爭之，安石怒，出通判真州。

translations.literal: Zongyu argued again; Anshi was angry and had him sent out as military prefect of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyu pressed the point again; Anshi, enraged, posted him as military prefect of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷提點河東刑獄、開封府推官、吏部右司郎中。

translations.literal: He successively served as judicial intendant of Hedong, investigating magistrate of Kaifeng, and right-section director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as judicial intendant of Hedong, investigating magistrate of Kaifeng, and right-section director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，進起居郎、中書舍人、給事中、御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was promoted to attendant gentleman, drafting secretary of the Secretariat, recipient of edicts, and censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou he rose to attendant gentleman, drafting secretary, recipient of edicts, and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時更定役法，書成，衙校募不足者，聽差入等戶。

translations.literal: At that time the corvée labor law was being revised; when the text was finished, where yamen runners could not be fully recruited, households of higher corvée grades were allowed to be conscripted in their place.
translations.idiomatic: While the corvée statutes were being rewritten, the draft allowed higher-grade households to be pressed into service wherever yamen runners could not be fully hired.

sentences.zh: 宗愈言：「法貴均一，若持兩端，則於文有害。

translations.literal: Zongyu said, "The law values uniformity; if one holds to two standards, the text is harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyu said, "Law must be even-handed; two faces in one clause corrupt the statute.

sentences.zh: 是乃差法，非募法也。

translations.literal: This is the conscription rule, not the recruitment rule.
translations.idiomatic: That belongs to conscription, not to hired service.

sentences.zh: 請刪之。」

translations.literal: I ask that it be deleted."
translations.idiomatic: Strike that passage."

sentences.zh: 哲宗嘗問朋黨之弊，對曰：「君子指小人為奸，則小人指君子為黨。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong once asked about the harm of factionalism; he replied, "When gentlemen call petty men wicked, petty men call gentlemen a faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong once asked about the evil of factions; Zongyu answered, "When the upright denounce schemers as corrupt, the schemers denounce the upright as a clique.

sentences.zh: 君子，蓋義之與比者。

translations.literal: Gentlemen are simply those who keep company with righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman keeps company with what is right—that is all.

sentences.zh: 陛下能擇中立之士而用之，則黨禍熄矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can choose and employ neutral-minded scholars, the scourge of factions will die out."
translations.idiomatic: Choose impartial scholars and put them to use, and factional strife will fade."

sentences.zh: 明日，具《君子無黨論》以進。

translations.literal: The next day he submitted in full his "Treatise on How Gentlemen Form No Faction."
translations.idiomatic: The following day he presented his complete essay "On How Gentlemen Form No Faction."

sentences.zh: 拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director of the right in the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the right in the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 於是諫議大夫王覿論其不當，而劉安世、韓川、孫覺等合攻之，朝廷依違。

translations.literal: At that time Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee Wang Xi argued that the appointment was improper, and Liu Anshi, Han Chuan, Sun Jue, and others jointly attacked him; the court wavered.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Grandee Wang Xi then argued the promotion was wrong, and Liu Anshi, Han Chuan, Sun Jue, and others piled on; the court could not decide.

sentences.zh: 逾年，出覿潤州，而言者愈力。

translations.literal: After more than a year Xi was sent out to Runzhou, but the critics grew only louder.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Xi was posted to Runzhou, yet the accusers grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 乃罷為資政殿學士、知陳州，徙成都府，蜀人安其政。

translations.literal: Zongyu was then dismissed to academician of the Hall of Literary Glory and prefect of Chenzhou, transferred to Chengdu, where the people of Shu were secure under his rule.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyu was stripped of his central post, made academician of the Hall of Literary Glory, and sent to Chenzhou, then to Chengdu, where the people of Shu found his governance reassuring.

sentences.zh: 召為禮部尚書，遷吏部，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: He was recalled as minister of Rites, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and died at age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as minister of Rites and then minister of Personnel, he died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈左銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was awarded Left Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Left Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 從子 宗回

translations.literal: Nephew Zonghui
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Zonghui

sentences.zh: 宗回，字醇夫，用蔭登第，為編修敕令官、司農寺幹當公事、京西轉運判官、提點刑獄、京東陝西轉運使、吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Zonghui, styled Chunfu, entered office by inherited privilege, passed the jinshi, and served as editor of edicts and statutes, handler of general business in the Ministry of Revenue, transport vice commissioner of the Western Capital circuit, judicial intendant, transport commissioner of the Eastern Capital and Shaanxi circuits, and director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui, courtesy name Chunfu, entered service by yin privilege and passed the jinshi; he served as editor of edicts and statutes, clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, Western Capital transport vice commissioner, judicial intendant, Eastern Capital and Shaanxi transport commissioner, and personnel director.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，以直龍圖閣知桂州，進寶文閣待制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng he was made prefect of Guizhou with the designation Straight Dragon Diagram, and advanced to awaiting edicts in the Hall of Treasured Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaosheng he became prefect of Guizhou with the Straight Dragon Diagram designation and was promoted to awaiting edicts in the Hall of Treasured Literature.

sentences.zh: 坐繫平民死，降集賢殿修撰、知隨州，改秦州、慶州，復為待制。

translations.literal: Because a commoner died in custody he was demoted to collator in the Hall of Gathered Worthies and prefect of Suizhou, then transferred to Qinzhou and Qingzhou, and again made awaiting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: After a detainee died in his custody he was reduced to collator in the Hall of Gathered Worthies and prefect of Suizhou, then served at Qinzhou and Qingzhou before regaining awaiting-edicts rank.

sentences.zh: 先是，熙河將王贍下邈川有功，帥孫路不樂贍，奪其兵與王愍。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Hexi general Wang Shan had taken Miaochuan with merit, but commander Sun Lu disliked Shan and stripped him of his troops, giving them to Wang Min.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Hexi general Wang Shan had captured Miaochuan with distinction, but commander Sun Lu resented him, seized his command, and gave the troops to Wang Min.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知之，以宗回代路，加直學士。

translations.literal: When the court learned of this, Zonghui replaced Lu and was given the added title of academician.
translations.idiomatic: The court learned of it and sent Zonghui to replace Lu, adding the title of academician.

sentences.zh: 時青唐瞎征內附，而心牟欽氈勒兵立別酋隴拶，還其地，勢復張。

translations.literal: At the time Xixia of Qingtang submitted to the court, but Xinmou Qinzhann raised troops and set up another chief, Longzan, restoring the territory, and their power swelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtang's Xixia ruler had submitted, but Xinmou Qinzhann rallied troops, installed the rival chief Longzan, and recovered the land, and their strength revived.

sentences.zh: 瞎征大懼，自髡為僧以祈免。

translations.literal: The Xixia ruler was greatly afraid and shaved his head to become a monk to pray for deliverance.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the Qingtang ruler tonsured himself as a monk to beg for mercy.

sentences.zh: 王贍怨孫路，因言青唐不煩兵可下。

translations.literal: Wang Shan, resenting Sun Lu, therefore said Qingtang could be taken without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shan, nursing a grudge against Sun Lu, claimed Qingtang could fall without a battle.

sentences.zh: 至，則駐宗哥城不進。

translations.literal: When he arrived he halted at Zongge City and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Zongge City and stalled there.

sentences.zh: 宗回怒，日夜檄趣之，且戒贍曰：「青唐兵甚弱，隴拶稚子，何能為，而怯懦逗遛，吾將以軍法從事。」

translations.literal: Zonghui was angry and day and night sent orders urging him on, and warned Shan, "Qingtang's troops are very weak; Longzan is a mere boy—what can he do? Yet you delay out of cowardice; I will treat you under military law."
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui fumed and bombarded him with dispatches, warning Shan: "Qingtang's forces are feeble and Longzan is a child—what threat is that? Your dithering is cowardice; I will invoke military law."

sentences.zh: 又遣王愍復至邈川，聲言代贍。

translations.literal: He also sent Wang Min back to Miaochuan, proclaiming that he would replace Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Min to Miaochuan again, publicly announcing that he would replace Shan.

sentences.zh: 贍懼，乃率步騎掩青唐，據之，隴拶降。

translations.literal: Shan was afraid and then led infantry and cavalry in a surprise attack on Qingtang, seized it, and Longzan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Shan finally led foot and horse in a raid on Qingtang, took the city, and Longzan submitted.

sentences.zh: 詔以青唐為鄯州，邈川為湟州。

translations.literal: An edict made Qingtang Shanzhou and Miaochuan Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed Qingtang as Shanzhou and Miaochuan as Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，屬羌郎阿章叛，拒官軍。

translations.literal: Before long the Qiang Lang Azhang rebelled and resisted the official army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Qiang leader Lang Azhang rebelled and fought the government forces.

sentences.zh: 宗回遣將王吉、魏釗討之，皆敗死。

translations.literal: Zonghui sent the generals Wang Ji and Wei Zhao to suppress him; both were defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui dispatched Wang Ji and Wei Zhao against him; both were routed and killed.

sentences.zh: 又遣鈐轄种朴往。

translations.literal: He again sent the deputy commander Zhong Pu.
translations.idiomatic: He next sent deputy commander Zhong Pu.

sentences.zh: 朴言：「賊鋒方銳，且盛寒，宜少緩師。」

translations.literal: Pu said, "The rebels' edge is sharp just now, and the cold is severe; the army ought to be slowed a little."
translations.idiomatic: Pu urged, "The enemy is at peak strength and the cold is bitter—we should pause the campaign."

sentences.zh: 宗回不聽，督之急。

translations.literal: Zonghui would not listen and pressed him urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui refused to listen and drove him hard.

sentences.zh: 朴不得已行，亦敗死。

translations.literal: Pu had no choice but to go, and was again defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Pu marched against his judgment and was killed in another defeat.

sentences.zh: 於是轉運判官秦希甫言湟、鄯難守，以為棄之便。

translations.literal: Thereupon transport vice commissioner Qin Xifu said Huang and Shan were hard to hold and that abandoning them would be advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Transport vice commissioner Qin Xifu then argued that Huangzhou and Shanzhou could not be held and ought to be given up.

sentences.zh: 事下宗回，宗回持不可，希甫罷去。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to Zonghui; Zonghui insisted it could not be done, and Xifu was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal went to Zonghui, who held firm against withdrawal, and Xifu was removed.

sentences.zh: 會徽宗棄鄯州，於是任伯雨再疏其罪，奪職知蘄州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong later abandoned Shanzhou, Ren Boyu again memorialized listing his crimes, and he was stripped of office and made prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong later abandoned Shanzhou, Ren Boyu renewed the charges; Zonghui lost his post and was sent to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 還，為待制。

translations.literal: On returning he was again made awaiting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he regained awaiting-edicts status.

sentences.zh: 歷慶、渭、陳、延、澶州。

translations.literal: He successively served at Qing, Wei, Chen, Yan, and Chan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Qing, Wei, Chen, Yan, and Chan.

sentences.zh: 兄宗愈入黨籍，宗回亦罷郡。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Zongyu was entered on the faction roll, Zonghui was also removed from his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother Zongyu was listed among the faction offenders, Zonghui too was dismissed from his post.

sentences.zh: 居亡何，錄其堅守湟、鄯之議，起知秦州。

translations.literal: Not long after, his steadfast argument for holding Huang and Shan was recorded, and he was raised again to be prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the court recalled his stubborn defense of Huang and Shan and restored him as prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 進樞密直學士，徙永興、鄭州、成德軍，復坐事去。

translations.literal: He was advanced to academician of the Privy Council, transferred to Yongxing, Zhengzhou, and the Chengde army, and again removed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Privy Council academician, he served at Yongxing, Zhengzhou, and Chengde, then lost office again over another matter.

sentences.zh: 大觀中卒，贈銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died in the Daguang era and was posthumously awarded Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Daguang reign and was posthumously granted Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 胡氏自宿始大，及宗愈仍世執政，其後子孫至侍從、九卿者十數，遂為晉陵名族。

translations.literal: From Su the Hu clan first grew great; through Zongyu they held power for generations, and afterward their descendants reaching attendant and the nine ministers numbered more than ten, until they became a famous clan of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu rose to prominence beginning with Su; through Zongyu they governed for generations, and later their line produced more than ten attendants and ministers of the nine courts, making Jinling's Hu a household name.

sentences.zh: 論曰：張昪清忠諒直，趙槩雅量過人，胡宿學通天人之奧，考其立朝大節，皆磊落為良執政。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Zhang Fang was pure, loyal, trustworthy, and upright; Zhao Gai's magnanimity surpassed others; Hu Su's learning penetrated the mysteries of Heaven and man—in examining their great integrity in office, all stood forthright as good chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Zhang Fang was incorruptible and bluntly honest; Zhao Gai's breadth of spirit stood above the crowd; Hu Su's learning reached into Heaven and human affairs—each, judged by his conduct at court, was an upright statesman.

sentences.zh: 宗愈仍居右轄，而學術視宿則有間矣。

translations.literal: Zongyu still held the right vice-directorship, yet in scholarship compared with Su there was a gap.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyu still sat among the highest ministers, but beside Su's learning he fell short.

sentences.zh: 宗回非邊將材，其守河湟之議，蓋以趣种朴於死，蘄合上意，以解其責爾。

translations.literal: Zonghui was no material for a frontier general; his argument for holding the He-Huang region was probably to drive Zhong Pu to his death, fit the emperor's wish, and shift blame from himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui was no frontier commander; his insistence on holding the Huang-Shan corridor likely hurried Zhong Pu to his death, pleased the throne, and let him dodge responsibility.

sentences.zh: 若胡氏之世大也，殆脫萬人於水死，而陰德之所致與？

translations.literal: As for the Hu clan's rise to greatness, was it perhaps because they pulled ten thousand people from drowning death, and hidden virtue brought it about?
translations.idiomatic: If the Hu grew great, perhaps it was because Su had snatched thousands from the flood—virtue unseen, reward deferred.
